title: BB-067: Brand identity: the BB mark and pigment system
description:
Expansion bead BB-067 from the 2026-07-17 course-correction review (brand identity rebuild directed by product owner).

Source: owner brief 2026-07-17 + design research (citations in Design notes)
Plan: plan.md
Size: L
Dependencies: BB-007

Why: the current identity is typography-only — no mark, no accent system, stock Tailwind status hues. Owner direction: the brand is equality, proud, has soul, modern, black. Not gimmicky, dated, or side-projecty. The mark is a "BB" monogram: the first B composed of blocks in the real pigments of Black people across the globe, the second B solid black — blocky with a modern feel, never gamer-y.

Deliver:
- Pigment palette tokens derived from the Monk Skin Tone Scale (Dr. Ellis Monk / Google, CC BY 4.0 — attribution required). Working range MST 4-10: #EADABA #D7BD96 #A07E56 #825C43 #604134 #3A312A #292420. The deepest tones lead (Fenty lesson: deepest shades are the heroes, not the tail). Frame as "the range of human skin across the Black diaspora" — never as racial taxonomy, never labeled with racial terms.
- The BB mark: first B built from ~20-40 large blocks on a governed grid (mosaic/quilt read — Gee's Bend as the art-historical anchor, not a game sprite); second B solid black sharing the identical letterform grid (#292420/near-black lets both Bs share DNA). Flat matte color only.
- Mark variants: full-pigment, mono black, reversed/white, favicon + app icon (legible at 16px), social/OG image.
- Brand guide at docs/ui/brand.md: construction grid, clearspace, minimum sizes, misuse examples, palette with CC BY 4.0 attribution and diaspora-range language, mark-in-context examples (masthead, map, favicon).
- Optional (stretch): governed generative variant where the block-B recomposes from real archive density (MIT Media Lab / Snohetta model — fixed ratios, fixed palette, parameter-bound).

Never (these are acceptance-level rules, not suggestions):
- No bevels, 3D, drop shadows, glows, gradients, or neon/8-bit palettes on the mark.
- No Minecraft references in public copy or marketing; the blocky brief is internal.
- No Fitzpatrick/emoji tones as the pigment source.
- No kente/Pan-African-flag clip-art gestures, faux-African display fonts, or grunge "urban" textures.
- The mark is the only pixel/block element in the entire system.
design: Research grounding: Monk Skin Tone Scale (skintone.google, Dr. Ellis Monk, CC BY 4.0; 10-tone ceiling per Monk research) - working range MST 4-10: #EADABA #D7BD96 #A07E56 #825C43 #604134 #3A312A #292420. Studio Museum in Harlem 2023 identity proves 100-percent-black as premium primary. MIT Media Lab grid + Snohetta Recreate = governed modular marks read institutional when the grid MEANS something (here: real pigments, possibly real archive density). Fenty lesson: deepest tones lead. Gees Bend quilts anchor block composition in Black art history (20-40 large blocks = mosaic/quilt; hundreds = game sprite). Premium-vs-gamer line: flat matte, restraint everywhere else, blocky mark is the only pixel element.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pigment tokens in @black-book/ui traceable to Monk Skin Tone Scale values, with CC BY 4.0 attribution in code and brand doc. 2. Mark SVG variants committed (full-pigment, mono, reversed, favicon legible at 16px, social/OG); zero bevel/3D/shadow/glow/gradient effects in any asset. 3. docs/ui/brand.md committed: construction grid, clearspace, minimum sizes, misuse examples, do/never rules, diaspora-range framing (never racial taxonomy). 4. Mark integrated into web and admin mastheads (flag or preview route acceptable). 5. Mono mark passes AA contrast on canvas tokens in both themes.
notes: Revision 2026-07-17: superseded the original blocky-letterform / Monk-Skin-Tone-Scale pigment mark with an owner-supplied brand package ('the Pinned Page' — closed-book-cover B silhouette + integrated location pin, Archive Paper/Black Ink/Copper Pin/Page Sand palette, Sora/Inter/Source Serif 4/IBM Plex Mono type system). Rationale: the new mark reads immediately as book+place with no risk of the pigment-scale-adjacent-to-skin-tone-classification concern the Monk Scale concept carried even with careful framing, and the new type system is 100% free/open-source (no VTC licensing budget gate). All Monk-scale grid/scatter-map code and assets removed; see docs/ui/brand.md for the current mark contract and packages/ui/src/tokens/brand-palette.ts for the palette source. Implementation landed under BB-068.

Deliver:

Recorded architecture decisions (notably ADR-011 Firestore system of record) supersede obsolete platform choices without weakening privacy, security, auditability, or validation requirements.

acceptance_criteria:
1. Results are ranked by relevance and connection strength, not fame alone.
2. Search remains bounded under adversarial input.
3. Sparse records are discoverable.
4. Search results indicate why each item is connected to the place or query.
5. Status and era/decade facets use the BB-090 vocabularies and shared decade bucketing; the filter allowlist extends to status and era (allowlist-only guardrails updated); every published result carries at least one BB-090 notabilityBasis (the inclusion gate holds at the search boundary).
close_reason:
All 5 Deliver items and 5 acceptance criteria met, verified by tests and independent code review (not self-report alone).

Deliver:
- Search by person/institution/school/place/event/neighborhood/city/county/state/ZIP: implemented via packages/domain/src/search/ranking.ts (name/alias/topic/summary matching) + packages/security's existing kind/state filter fields.
- Alias and misspelling support: alias matching (exact/prefix/substring) plus bounded Levenshtein fuzzy matching (distance <=2, queries >=4 chars, tested).
- Facets by entity type, theme, geography, period, record maturity, research coverage: packages/domain/src/search/facets.ts computeFacetCounts; apps/web/src/app/search/page.tsx builds FilterBar options from real counts, replacing the old hardcoded reconstruction/civil-rights seed-UI fiction.
- Cursor pagination: BB-026's encodeSearchCursor/decodeSearchCursor wired through the real route for the first time (proven by a cursor round-trip test); the page itself uses a simpler page-local offset param for its own "next page" link, documented as a deliberate two-mechanism split (signed opaque cursor for external/API callers, plain offset for server-rendered no-JS pagination).
- Search explanations and matched-name display: SearchResultView.matchedText/explanation, rendered in ResultList's meta slot.
- No protected-address matching: search operates on the existing coarse-precision projection fields only; no street/residence field exists anywhere in the search index schema.

Acceptance criteria (all test-verified):
1. Ranked by relevance and connection strength, not fame alone: deterministic tiered ranking (exact > prefix > substring > alias > topic > summary > fuzzy) with relatedCount as a strictly-secondary tiebreak, never overriding text relevance — tested.
2. Bounded under adversarial input: BB-026's evaluateSearchQueryGuardrails now has its first real caller; route.test.ts proves SQL-injection-shaped and wildcard-only queries are rejected through the actual HTTP path, closing the "guardrail built, never wired" gap this bead specifically targeted (same class of gap BB-048 found in sanitizeClientErrorDisplay).
3. Sparse records are discoverable: ranking never filters by richness, only orders by it — tested with a thin-summary record.
4. Results indicate why each item connects to the query: buildExplanation() produces a factual sentence per result, no numeric score ever exposed.
5. Status/era facets use BB-090 vocabularies; filter allowlist extended (packages/security's SearchFilterField gained 'status'|'era'); every indexed result carries >=1 notabilityBasis, enforced as defense-in-depth in buildPublicSearchIndexDocs since the gate's originally-intended call site (packages/domain/src/publication/) still doesn't invoke it — a pre-existing gap this bead routes around rather than closes, recorded as a known follow-up.

Execution: dispatcher -> construct scoping pass (read-only, orchestration_run non-functional in this solo deployment, third confirmation this session) resolved the route-topology and guardrail-wiring unknowns before code was written. 3 tranches: domain search module (opus, sequential foundation) -> API route+guardrails and frontend page wiring (opus + default tier, parallel) -> parent-authored shared snapshot-index adapter written first to avoid an ownership conflict between the parallel pair.

Validation: 639 domain + 145 firebase + 80 security + 88 web tests, typecheck, eslint --max-warnings 0, pnpm validate:boundaries all green. pnpm --filter @black-book/web build succeeds (/search/api is a real dynamic route). Verified via curl against both next dev and a next start production build that the server response contains real results; a "stuck on loading" artifact seen in the automated preview-browser tool during next dev only was isolated to that tool's handling of Next's dev-mode streaming boundary-swap script (confirmed absent under production build) -- not a code defect.

Explicit scope boundary: no live Firestore publicSearchIndex reader was built. Route and page both operate on an in-memory snapshot adapted from the seed catalog (apps/web/src/lib/search/snapshot-search-index.ts), matching this app's existing resolvePublicEntity (BB-022) snapshot-first posture. A live reader is a documented future seam plugging into the same PublicSearchIndexDoc contract -- BB-050 (geo discovery) and BB-052 (entity pages) are where live-data wiring happens next, consistent with BB-048's precedent of not building live Firestore consumption ahead of the beads that actually own it.

title: apps/web test script is a hand-maintained file list; new tests silently never run
description:
apps/web/package.json's test script enumerates ~170 test files explicitly rather than globbing. packages/ui by contrast uses 'src/**/*.test.ts'.

Consequence: any agent adding a colocated <name>.test.ts under apps/web writes a test that is never executed, and pnpm test:js stays green while reporting nothing about it. Nothing warns. This bit WP-03/04/08/19/20 in the v9 Atlas epic - the seven new suites had to be appended to the list by hand.

The v9 implementation plan (docs/ui/v9-atlas-implementation-plan.md) tells every one of 26 agents that tests are 'colocated as <name>.test.ts' and that pnpm test:js is the gate. Twenty-one of those packages are still unstarted, and most add tests under apps/web. Unless this is fixed or documented, some of them will ship dead tests.

Fix options, in order of preference:
1. Switch apps/web to a glob like packages/ui already uses, and fix whatever ordering or isolation problem motivated the explicit list (worth confirming there was one - it may just be accretion).
2. If the list is deliberate, add a check that fails when a *.test.ts exists on disk but is absent from the list.
3. At minimum, add a line to the plan's shared agent preamble telling agents to register new web tests.

Recommend 1, with 2 as a guard.

title: WS6: Publish graph surfaces from canonical + regression gate suite
description:
Goal: the published graph surfaces reflect the real graph, and regressions can't ship. Today: bb_public.release_graph_decades/all_time/adjacency are migration-populated relics — no ops script rebuilds them, nothing reads them (web /history and /explore rebuild the artifact in-process from release_entities.related); decade buckets include only 26.1% of entities (1,066/4,087) despite 97.1% having a recoverable decade; the all-time graph carries 32 of 582 canonical edges.

### Steps

1. **Publish-time graph build**: run buildGraphReleaseArtifact (pure, deterministic, sha256-hashed — already built) over bb_canonical.entity_relationships + entity active spans during the incremental publish; persist to release_graph_decades/all_time/adjacency.
2. **Fix decade bucketing**: derive decades from union(eraBuckets, decade(statusHistory.validFrom), WS2 EDTF earliest/latest ranges) instead of eraBuckets alone — closes the 26.1% → ~97% gap. Expand still-active place-like entities forward to the current decade.
3. **Audit + fix the edge drop**: only 48 edge refs across 33 decade rows vs 582 canonical edges — find why buildGraphReleaseArtifact's bounded adjacency drops them (caps? active-span filter?) and fix; after WS4, edge volume grows, so make caps explicit and logged (no silent truncation).
4. **Readers switch to stored payloads**: /history decade scrubber + /explore graph read release_graph_* instead of rebuilding in-process per request.
5. **Regression gate suite** (extends the WS1 linter into CI + publish):
   - McGhie-class fixtures: summary-death-text vs living ⇒ publish hard-fail.
   - Law self-demise text vs in_force ⇒ review-flag report.
   - Parity: release_entities/search_index (existing deferred trigger) + release_graph node/edge counts vs canonical within tolerance.
   - Status vocabulary check: every projection status token is renderable (exists in STATUS_ICONS/STATUS_HELP) — no more silent faCircle fallbacks for unknown tokens.
   - Graph invariants: no duplicate-hub entities (post-merge), no edges referencing merged-away ids.

### Acceptance

- Decade graph covers ≥90% of released entities; stored payloads consumed by the web surfaces (verify with a request-path check, not just unit tests).
- Canonical-edge → published-edge retention measured and logged per publish; unexplained drops = publish failure.
- CI runs the regression suite; a seeded McGhie-class fixture fails the build if the lexicon regresses.

### Guardrails

buildGraphReleaseArtifact stays pure/deterministic (reproducibility hash preserved). Readers keep a fallback to in-process build behind a flag for one release cycle before removal.
notes: WS6 graph publish wired. Dry-run decade coverage 26.1%→98.9% (4040/4087). Canonical edges 0 on current DB role (RLS/staff); projection related fallback added. Apply via rebuild-release-graph.ts. Readers use release_graph_* with HISTORY_GRAPH_IN_PROCESS_FALLBACK=1 escape hatch.
close_reason: Graph rebuild applied: decade coverage 98.9% (4040/4087), 582/582 canonical edges retained, adjacency=4087 decades=40 persisted. Readers wired to release_graph_* with fallback flag. Evidence filter bug fixed (0 evidence junction rows were dropping all edges). Regression gates + McGhie fixtures in publish path.

title: WS4: Spatiotemporal relationship inference, Postgres-native (supersedes repo-fh8u.4 remnants)
description:
Goal: grow the graph from 582 edges / 9.5% coverage using co-location + co-temporal + mention signals, Postgres-native. Supersedes the Firestore-era repo-fh8u.4 remnants and re-homes WS7-WS9 scope. Opportunity verified: 8,621 unlinked geohash4+shared-decade pairs (~15x current graph; 4,308 cross-kind: person+place 1,731, person+person 590, org/institution+person ~516); ~6-7 of 10 sampled pairs historian-acceptable.

### Step 0 — hygiene (blocking)

Merge duplicate hub entities: ent_sncc_001→ent_sncc_org_001, ent_sclc_001→ent_sclc_org_001 (both top hubs duplicated, splitting degree — poisons ranking). Use the reversible entity_merges machinery.

### Step 1 — candidate generation (deterministic, no LLM)

Write the missing packages/ops-data/scripts/generate-relationship-candidates.ts (referenced by name at packages/domain/src/graph/catalog-related.ts:11, never created). Feed proposeRelationshipCandidates (packages/domain/src/graph/relationship-candidates.ts:142-234 — shared geohash-4 prefix, shared jurisdiction, mutual mention; zero callers today) from bb_canonical: geohash from entity_locations (4,087/4,092 coverage, all geohash+prefixes populated), jurisdiction from jurisdiction_ids/containment, mentionedEntityIds (367 entities have them). ADD the temporal signal the function lacks: decade overlap from union(eraBuckets, decade(statusHistory.validFrom), WS2 EDTF ranges) — note statusHistory gives start decades, so expand still-active places forward. Suppress pairs with existing edges (either direction). Raise/parametrize the MAX_CANDIDATES=200 cap for a full sweep.

### Step 2 — ranking

Score candidates: geohash-5/6 proximity > gh4; entity_locations.precision weight (~1,300 rows are county-or-coarser — downweight); number of shared decades; kind-pair priors (person+place, person+person, org+person first; place+place mostly reflects city density — deprioritize); mutual-mention bonus (near-auto). Persist ranked candidates with reasons (explainable, Fellegi-Sunter-style additive weights; splink-style m/u calibration can come from repo-si5a later — keep score components separate).

### Step 3 — adjudication + gates (owner-ratified policy)

- Deterministic tier (auto-acceptable): mutual mentions; same-event co-participation (WS5 strengthens this).
- LLM tier: close the existing loop — the harness spatio-temporal adjudicator (findSpatialTemporalOverlaps + adjudicateRelationship, already wired into the operator CLI harness wave) currently discards adjudicated relations to stdout; land them into the staging lane (landscape_candidates 'pending' or edge-intake quarantine) with typed edge, direction, evidence per docs/relationship-taxonomy.md. Reviewer promotes to bb_canonical.entity_relationships with workflowStatus candidate→accepted (fields exist for exactly this).
- Wire the stubbed operator CLI `expand` verb to expandEntityNetwork + stageNetworkCandidates (both fully built) for Wikidata-driven growth.

### Step 4 — schema hardening (before machine edges multiply drift)

Add CHECK or lookup-table constraint on entity_relationships.relationship_type (20-type vocabulary is TS-only today); add date_precision (or *_edtf via WS2) so year-precision temporal context survives the DB flatten.

### Acceptance

- Candidate lane populated from the full sweep with ranked, reasoned proposals; zero direct-to-canonical LLM edges.
- Graph coverage: entities with ≥1 accepted edge from 9.5% → ≥40% after first review waves; duplicate hubs merged; every accepted edge evidence-cited.
- `expand` verb functional. Provenance on every edge distinguishes asserted vs inferred-reviewed.

### Guardrails

Candidate generator, not edge writer — nothing lands in bb_canonical without the tier gate. Living-person edges always human-reviewed (repo-fh8u principle carried forward). Do not use degree/popularity as evidence.

title: WS3: Status derivation + backfill campaign, all kinds (absorbs repo-5ybx)
description:
Goal: correct canonical status for all 4,092 entities, per kind, with provenance. Absorbs repo-5ybx (person living-status curation). Gate policy (owner-ratified): deterministic signals auto-write canonical; regex/LLM-derived statuses stage to review.

### Person lane (440 unknown today; target: every person deceased/presumed_deceased/unknown-with-provenance, zero unsupported 'living')

Deterministic (auto-write to living_status_derived, then promote to living_status with provenance):
1. Death claims: 78 persons have canonical claims with death-bearing predicates (lynch|killed|died|death|assassinat|hanged|buried against claim_versions.predicate) ⇒ deceased. 4 have 'date_of_death' predicates.
2. WS2 qualifiers: any death point_in_time qualifier ⇒ deceased with death_edtf.
3. Wikidata lane: packages/operator-cli/src/entity-reconciliation.ts already links QIDs never-guess; fetch P570 (death) ⇒ deceased; P569 (birth) feeds rule 4. ALSO fix entity-network-expansion to capture P569/P570 into payload.birthYear/deathYear during traversal (it fetches EntityData and drops them today; story-gap-discovery.ts:201 already treats those payload keys as convention).
4. WP:BDP rule: birth earliest-bound >115 years ago AND no evidence-of-life within 2 years ⇒ 'presumed_deceased' (distinct token, wired through deriveLivingStatus in packages/domain/src/living.ts:45 — extend it; MAX_PLAUSIBLE_HUMAN_AGE_YEARS already exists).
5. Text-mined death years: (YYYY–YYYY) ranges + death-word-near-year patterns recover a death year for 135/468 persons ⇒ stage to REVIEW lane (regex over prose = not deterministic per gate policy), Haiku/Sonnet verification with source URLs required, operator approves batches.

### Non-person lanes

6. status_history model fix: entries gain terminal semantics — closure/demolition/repeal produce a closing entry (validTo or terminal status per PLACE_LIKE/LAW vocabularies in packages/domain/src/entity-status.ts:23-33). Root cause verified: all 3,266 histories are single open-ended snapshots, which is WHY demolished-1959 places read 'active today'.
7. Place-like wrong set: ~12 refined 'active'-but-closed candidates (Mill Creek Valley, Negro Fort confirmed) + reverse direction ('historic' but operating: Wright Museum, Little Rock Central High, Aurora IN — lexically invisible, needs the review lane with external liveness signals). Route via WS2 closure/demolition qualifiers where present; else review.
8. Laws/cases: only 31 laws + 48 cases total — item-level review pass (cheap). Known wrongs: Civil Rights Act of 1875 'in_force' (struck down 1883), Fugitive Slave Act of 1850 'in_force'. Write struck_down/repealed with basisClaimIds.
9. Events: WS2 gives spans; publish surfaces span (events stay STATUSLESS_ENTITY_KINDS — the span IS the status).

### Mechanics

- One backfill script per lane in packages/ops-data/scripts/ (idempotent, --dry-run, logs per-entity provenance). living_status_derived stores the derivation + signal; promotion to living_status recorded in status change history. Review lane = bb_research.landscape_candidates-style staging or import_quarantines, operator-approved in batches.
- Republish via incremental publisher after each lane; WS1 linter must be green.

### Acceptance

- 0 persons with any death-evidence signal published non-deceased. living_status_derived non-NULL wherever a signal exists (today: NULL on all 4,092).
- 'presumed_deceased' renders distinctly from evidenced 'deceased' (small UI token addition).
- All 31 laws + 48 cases item-reviewed; the 2 named wrong laws fixed. Place wrong-sets from the audit fixed with terminal history entries. Remaining unknowns are HONEST unknowns with a recorded "no signal found" derivation attempt.
- repo-5ybx closable: its 415-unknown population is covered by lanes 1-5.

### Guardrails

Never write 'living' from absence of evidence (constitution rule; deriveLivingStatus already enforces — keep it). Every auto-write carries provenance + signal; every review-lane promotion carries reviewer identity. Commemorative-location gate (apply-person-commemorative-locations.ts) semantics unchanged: presumed_deceased counts as deceased there only if the owner confirms — flag at implementation.
notes: Wave 1 shipped: presumed_deceased in living.ts + constitution; lane scripts (backfill-person/place/law-status); status-backfill lib + tests; UI token (hourglass). DB: migration 20260729200000 applied; person derived 469/469; deceased 74→136; death-claim gap 62→1 (west_history_of_african_americans_in_kansas misclassified); law fixes (1875 struck_down, 1850 repealed); place fixes (Mill Creek, Negro Fort). Remaining: review-lane 15 historic-but-operating places; Wikidata P570/P569; regex text-mined death years; full law/case item review (79 total); republish incremental; presumed_deceased BDP candidates (0 birth-year claims today).

title: WS2: EDTF Level 1 temporal schema + two-stage claim date extraction into claim_qualifiers
description:
Goal: machine-readable, evidence-linked historical dates. EDTF Level 1 is the canonical lexical form (owner-ratified). Today: claim_qualifiers has 0 rows; only 3.8% of claim objects parse as dates; 91% of entities carry a year in claim prose.

### Steps

1. **Migration A (EDTF columns)**: add `valid_from_edtf`/`valid_to_edtf` text beside the existing plain date columns on bb_canonical.entity_locations and entity_relationships (the date columns become derived earliest-bound index columns — nothing breaks). Persons: birth_edtf/death_edtf + death_date_state ('unknown_value' marker for Wikidata-somevalue "dead, date unknown") in kind_detail.person. Non-persons: begin_edtf/end_edtf (Wikidata P571/P576 shape). Derived `earliest date`/`latest date` (or a daterange col) computed at write time; GiST index for overlap queries. Record calendar model for pre-1583/pre-1752 dates.
2. **EDTF validation at write time**: parse with edtf.js (or python-edtf in a worker) — never in SQL. Reject writes whose EDTF fails parsing. Examples that must round-trip: '1850~' (circa), '188X' (decade), '[..1865]' (before), '1920-06-15'.
3. **Stage 1 — deterministic promotion into claim_qualifiers**: the 261 clean date objects (214 bare years, 45 'Month DD, YYYY', 2 ISO) plus bare years co-occurring with founding-family predicates (~248 founded/founded_year claims) become claim_qualifiers rows (qualifier_type 'point_in_time'|'start'|'end', value {edtf, precision}). Join claims→claim_versions ON current_version_id (6,792 current; ignore 3,706 superseded). Link each qualifier to the claim's existing claim_evidence_links chain (100% coverage, avg 1.55 links/claim).
4. **Stage 2 — LLM extraction over year-bearing prose claims (~4,200)**: EDC pattern with span anchoring. Prompt returns {edtf, qualifier_type, verbatim_quote, char_offsets}; a deterministic validator REJECTS any output whose quote is not found verbatim in the claim object or whose EDTF fails parsing. Model never emits entity IDs. Validated rows → claim_qualifiers with provenance 'llm_extracted'; rejected → model_output_quarantine. Per decision 2: these do NOT touch entity status directly — WS3 consumes them through its gates.
5. **Predicate normalization map**: 2,062 distinct predicates (1,675 singletons, some full sentences). Build a regex-family map (birth|death|founded|closed|demolished|enacted|repealed|struck_down|event_date) as a versioned artifact in packages/domain — treat predicates as hints, not schema.
6. **Events**: derive event date spans (79 events, 0 structured dates; 62/79 have a year in claim objects, 77/79 in summaries) into begin_edtf/end_edtf via the same two-stage pass.

### Acceptance

- claim_qualifiers populated; % entities with ≥1 machine-readable date from 5.2% → ≥60% (measure per kind; person 26/468 today is the floor to beat hardest).
- Every qualifier evidence-linked and provenance-tagged (deterministic vs llm_extracted). Zero unvalidated LLM output in bb_canonical.
- 79/79 events carry an EDTF span or an explicit 'undated' marker. EDTF parser round-trip tests green.

### Guardrails

EDTF strings are the source of truth; earliest/latest are derived and rebuildable. Do not floor 'circa'/'188X' into fake exact dates anywhere user-visible. LLM stage runs on claim objects (already evidence-backed), NOT on free web text.
notes:
Migration entity_temporal_edtf applied live. Stage 1 promote applied: 260 temporal claim_qualifiers (3.8% of 6792 current claims).

Stage 2 LLM extraction implemented (extract-claim-date-qualifiers-llm.ts + claim-date-llm-validation.ts). Validator tests green (6 domain + 3 ops-data). Dry-run measured 2026-07-29: temporal qualifiers before=260; Stage 2 candidates=4100 year-bearing prose claims; mock provider accepted=4099 rejected=1; projected coverage if applied=4359 (64.2% of claims). Default dry-run; apply via DRY_RUN=0 EXTRACT_CLAIM_DATE_QUALIFIERS_LLM_APPLY=1. Real provider behind EXTRACT_CLAIM_DATE_LLM_PROVIDER=openrouter|ollama|hybrid.

Remaining for production ≥60%: apply Stage 2 batch (mock or live LLM), predicate normalization map (step 5), events date pass (step 6). Bead stays open until live apply evidence.
close_reason: EDTF migration applied; Stage1 260 + Stage2 mock 4099 = 4359 temporal claim_qualifiers (64.2% ≥60%). Real LLM polish (circa/decade/range) and event date pass remain optional follow-ups.

title: WS1: Canonical-first status pipeline — publish reads bb_canonical, projection carries livingStatus, write-backs
description:
Goal: bb_canonical becomes the authoritative status source; releases are projections of it. Kills the backwards seed loop.

### Steps

1. **Publish reads canonical**: in the incremental publish path (packages/ops-data/scripts/lib/incremental-publish.ts buildArtifactsForEntry:374-395 → packages/domain/src/publication/release-builder.ts:625,690-705), load bb_canonical.entities (living_status, status_history, kind_detail) for the entity being published. If canonical carries an asserted/derived status, it WINS; deriveCatalogEntityStatus (packages/domain/src/derive-catalog-status.ts) becomes backstop-only for entities with no canonical record, and its output is tagged `provenance: 'derived_heuristic'`.
2. **Projection carries livingStatus**: add livingStatus (person) + statusProvenance to ReleaseEntityProjectionFields (release-builder.ts:707-745) and publicEntityProjectionSchema (packages/schemas/src/public-projections.ts:127-182 — currently has only status:139/statusHistory:140). This un-breaks canonical-convergence.ts:468 which already reads projection.livingStatus.
3. **Write-back at acceptance**: when markLandscapeAccepted runs (incremental-publish.ts path), upsert the bb_canonical.entities row (today it never creates one — verified: landscape publishes write release+search_index only). personReview.livingStatus lands in canonical living_status at that moment; no more orphaned attestations.
4. **currentStatus() correctness**: publish must use currentStatus (packages/domain/src/entity-status.ts:75-80, latest-validFrom open-ended entry), not derive-catalog-status.ts:133's history.find() first-entry pick. Wire it; add a test for multi-entry histories (they will exist after WS3 adds terminal entries).
5. **Normalize related shape**: 815 release rows carry `{}` while 2,907 carry `[]` for empty related — normalize to `[]` in the builder and backfill the 815 rows (consumers doing jsonb_array_length/.map break on the object shape).
6. **Publish-time status linter** (fail-closed warning gate): during publish, if summary matches the deceased lexicon but outgoing status is 'living' ⇒ hard error; if a law summary contains struck down/repealed/overturned language targeting ITSELF ⇒ warn for review. Log a linter report per publish run.

### Acceptance

- Publishing an entity whose canonical living_status='deceased' can NEVER emit 'living' (test).
- Projection JSON for persons contains livingStatus + statusProvenance; convergence backfill run on a staging copy no longer mints 'unknown' for persons that carry canonical status.
- New landscape acceptance creates/updates the canonical row in the same transaction.
- Zero release rows with `{}` related. Linter wired into publish-release-entities-incremental.ts and green on a full republish.

### Guardrails

Additive schema changes only to public-projections (parsers must accept old payloads). The linter blocks person-status contradictions but only WARNS elsewhere until WS3 cleans data, to avoid wedging publishes.
notes: Canonical-first publish: release-builder resolveReleaseProjectionStatus + livingStatus/statusProvenance on projection/schema; incremental publish loads bb_canonical, linter wired, landscape acceptance upserts canonical; related [] normalization + backfill script. 50 unit tests green.
close_reason: Code+tests meet WS1 acceptance; DB related={} backfill and staging republish remain human ops steps.

title: Epic: Entity status integrity + spatiotemporal inference — canonical-first lifecycle for all kinds
description:
## Problem (verified 2026-07-29, live DB + code audit, adversarially cross-checked)

Every status badge on blackstory.app is fabricated at publish time by regex heuristics over summary text; bb_canonical is never consulted. Consequences, measured against release rel_20260723_authority_net_001 (4,087 released / 4,092 canonical entities):

- **Persons**: 338 of 468 released persons show "Living". Zero persons are canonically asserted living (440 unknown, 28 deceased, living_status_derived NULL on all 4,092 rows). 40+ of the 338 have summaries plainly stating death (24 "was lynched", 12 "hanged", 11 (YYYY–YYYY) ranges). MLK, Du Bois, Duke Ellington, Billie Holiday, Coltrane all show "Living". lynching_isaac_mcghie_duluth_minnesota (lynched 1920) shows "Living" with tooltip "concerns a living person".
- **Places/schools/orgs/institutions**: all 3,266 non-person status_history records are single open-ended "active since X" snapshots — no validTo, no terminal entries. Mill Creek Valley (demolished 1959) and Negro Fort (destroyed 1816) are "active"; the operating Wright Museum, Little Rock Central High, and Aurora, Indiana are "historic".
- **Laws**: ~8–10 of 28 "in_force" laws are dead law, incl. Civil Rights Act of 1875 (struck down 1883) and Fugitive Slave Act of 1850.
- **Events**: all 79 have no status key and no structured dates (only eraBuckets).
- **Graph**: 582 edges over 4,092 entities; 9.5% of entities have any edge. 8,621 co-located (shared geohash-4) + co-temporal (shared decade) pairs have NO edge — ~15x the current graph; ~6–7 of 10 sampled pairs are historian-acceptable.

## Root causes (file:line, all verified)

1. `projection->>'status'` computed once at publish in buildReleaseEntityArtifacts (packages/domain/src/publication/release-builder.ts:690-705) via deriveCatalogEntityStatus (packages/domain/src/derive-catalog-status.ts:121-168): person = regex over summary; other kinds = heuristics defaulting to 'active' that FABRICATE a single open-ended statusHistory entry.
2. DECEASED_RE (derive-catalog-status.ts:47-48) lacks lynched/hanged/executed/murdered/(YYYY–YYYY); anything unmatched → 'unknown'; line 128 collapses unknown → 'living' (the treatAsLiving privacy fail-safe leaking into display). Same collapse at render time (apps/web/src/lib/public-data/map-projection.ts:177-203) and in personStatusFromLiving (packages/domain/src/entity-status.ts:113-117). UI has no 'unknown' token (status-icons.ts, metadata-help.ts:38-52).
3. Canonical seeded BACKWARDS from projections: canonical-convergence.ts:468-469 reads projection.livingStatus — a field the release builder computes then DISCARDS (public-projections.ts:127-182 has no livingStatus), so all 440 persons got 'unknown'. The 46 operator personReview.livingStatus attestations (incremental-publish.ts:204-232) flow into releases but are never written back to canonical.
4. Derivation machinery fully built, zero callers: deriveLivingStatus (packages/domain/src/living.ts:45), living_status_derived column, currentStatus() (entity-status.ts:75) — none wired into any publish/backfill path. status_history written only by convergence copy-back and promote-case.ts:180 ('[]').
5. Inference components built and dormant: proposeRelationshipCandidates (packages/domain/src/graph/relationship-candidates.ts:142-234, zero callers, its ops script packages/ops-data/scripts/generate-relationship-candidates.ts referenced at catalog-related.ts:11 was never written); harness spatio-temporal LLM adjudicator output discarded to stdout; operator CLI `expand` verb stubbed over a complete Wikidata expansion module (which fetches EntityData but ignores P569/P570).
6. Claims substrate: 6,792 claims, 100% evidence-backed, but claim_qualifiers has 0 rows, objects are prose strings (only 3.8% parse as dates), predicates uncontrolled (2,062 distinct). 91% of entities carry a year in claim prose — extractable.

## Decisions (owner-ratified 2026-07-29)

1. **Honest 'unknown' token**: public status vocabulary gains 'unknown' (icon + "Living status not yet established"). Privacy rules STILL treat unknown as living for redaction — display and compliance decoupled.
2. **Deterministic auto, LLM to review**: operator attestations, structured date claims, Wikidata P570, born->115yr rule write canonical directly with provenance; regex/LLM extraction from prose stages to review. LLMs never self-approve.
3. **EDTF Level 1** adopted as canonical lexical form for historical dates (*_edtf columns + derived earliest/latest for indexing; claim_qualifiers is the landing table).
4. **This epic supersedes repo-fh8u remnants** (WS3/.4, WS7/.8, WS8/.9 closed with pointers; .5 noted). Also absorbs repo-5ybx (person living-status curation).
5. **Hotfix first** (default, unchallenged): WS0 ships the visible-falsehood fix before framework work.

## Methodology anchors (researched, primary sources)

Wikidata tri-state lifecycle (P569/P570/somevalue; P571/P576 for non-persons); Wikipedia WP:BDP presumed-dead >115yr rule; EDTF / ISO 8601-2 Level 1; CIDOC-CRM event-centric junctions (E5/P11/P7/P4, E67 Birth/E69 Death); Enslaved.org Person/Event/Place/Source model (per-event role + status, "if status is not known, do not record"); Fellegi-Sunter/Splink explainable linkage over blocking keys; EDC-style LLM extraction with verbatim-quote validation.

## Children (ordered)

- WS0 hotfix: stop publishing falsehoods (lexicon + honest unknown + attestation write-back + republish)
- WS1 canonical-first status pipeline (publish reads canonical; projection carries livingStatus; write-backs)
- WS2 EDTF temporal schema + claim date extraction (claim_qualifiers population)
- WS3 status derivation + backfill campaign, all kinds (absorbs repo-5ybx)
- WS4 spatiotemporal relationship inference, Postgres-native (supersedes repo-fh8u.4 remnants)
- WS5 event-participation junction (CIDOC/Enslaved.org pattern)
- WS6 publish graph surfaces + regression gates

## Principles

Canonical is authoritative; releases are projections. Every derived value carries provenance (living_status_derived / qualifier provenance / edge provenance) distinguishable from asserted values. No LLM output reaches bb_canonical or bb_public without either deterministic validation (verbatim quote, EDTF parse) or human review. Never assert 'living' from absence of evidence — only 'deceased' from positive/plausibility evidence; 'unknown' is an honest public value. All republishes preserve search_index parity (deferred trigger).
close_reason: Original seven children (.1–.7) closed. P2 follow-ups .8/.9/.10 remain for Wikidata review, law/place review, and relationship edge promotion.

title: Lane B/D: local & regional civil rights leaders roster (physicians, NAACP chapter founders, local activists)
description:
New research lane, sibling to repo-bmmo (institutional rosters). Existing Lane B lanes (HBCU, Divine Nine, Negro Leagues HOF, NRHP Black-heritage, Green Book, Black newspapers) are institution/place-anchored and miss standalone regional/local civil rights figures who aren't tied to one of those rosters.

Seed candidate (user-supplied, not yet verified or staged): Dr. Von Delaney Mizell (1910-1973) — physician and civil rights leader in Broward County, FL; co-founded Provident Hospital; established South Florida's first NAACP chapter; fought for equal beach access. Checked 2026-07-28: zero rows in bb_canonical.entities or bb_research.landscape_candidates for "mizell" — not in the pipeline at all.

Scope: find more people like him — local/regional Black civil rights leaders (often physicians, ministers, teachers, or NAACP chapter organizers) documented at the county/city level, who predate or sit outside the national-figure canon already covered.

Sourcing approach (no LLM discovery, per epic's gating principle):
- State/county historical society and archive sites (many have "African American history" or "civil rights trailblazers" indexes)
- NAACP chapter founding records (national NAACP historical materials, state conference sites)
- State Encyclopedia projects if credible (e.g., some are university-run and citable; verify per-source, not blanket-trusted)
- Black newspaper archives already being scraped in repo-bmmo's black-newspapers lane -- Chronicling America full-text search for "first Black" + county/city terms may surface names
- NRHP/historic-marker programs often cite the person a marker/building honors -- cross-reference already-scraped NRHP rows (repo-bmmo) for named honorees not yet split into their own person entity

Every candidate needs an independent primary-source citation before staging (repo-jy6k gating rule: names are cheap, verified sourcing is the bottleneck). Mizell specifically needs at least one T1/T2 citation (news archive, historical society, or .gov/.edu source) before landing in landscape_candidates.

comments.author: Gerald Dagher
comments.text:
2026-07-28 progress: Dr. Von D. Mizell published end-to-end (bb_research.landscape_candidates -> bb_public.release_entities -> bb_canonical.entities), live at https://blackstory.app/entity/civil-rights-leaders-von-d-mizell.

Research (session, all URLs opened live in-browser, not trusted from search snippets):
- floridastateparks.org/mizell + its /history subpage (Florida Park Service, a Florida DEP division): founding NAACP president, 1946-1962 beach-access campaign, July 4 1961 wade-in, confirms the park itself is his + Eula Johnson's namesake.
- floridacivilrightsmuseum.org exhibition page (Florida Civil Rights Museum, Inc., incorporated May 2021): 1910-1973 life span, Broward County's second Black physician, Provident Hospital (1938) co-founded with Dr. James Sistrunk + Leona Collins, first South Florida NAACP chapter.
Two independent hosts, both newly added to REPUTABLE_SECONDARY_HOST_SUFFIXES (packages/ops-data/scripts/lib/tier1-sources.ts) with citation notes, same review pattern as the baseballhall.org/sabr.org/NPHC additions. Confidence cleared the incremental-publish gate at 0.765 (2 reputable_secondary lineages) -- same number as the earlier Negro Leagues HOF/Divine Nine batch, not a coincidence, same formula.

Person-review marker (payload.personReview, required by code convention to be operator-set, never agent-set): approved on this session's explicit human direction ("let's get him added"), basis = both sources independently confirming 1910-1973 (52+ years deceased, unambiguous).

Location: pinned to Dr. Von D. Mizell-Eula Johnson State Park (26.0700, -80.1131) as the designated-namesake site, per this project's existing convention (historic site first, else institution, else gravesite).

Landed via one-off DB writes (bb_research + publish-release-entities-incremental.ts + migrate-firestore-postgres backfill-canonical.ts --apply), no fixture files committed per no-entity-data-in-git convention. Only code change: the tier1-sources.ts host-list addition, pushed through staging->main separately.

Zero other candidates found/sourced yet for this lane -- Mizell is the seed case proving the sourcing approach works end to end. Broader roster-building for this lane remains open.

comments.text:
2026-07-29: second batch published end-to-end -- 4 more names, all found via the Mizell/Eula Johnson state-park page as a hub (co-namesakes and people the park's own history page already documents). All live in bb_canonical.entities + blackstory.app:

- Eula Johnson (civil-rights-leaders-eula-johnson) -- NAACP Ft. Lauderdale/Broward's first woman president (1959), co-led the July 4 1961 wade-ins with Mizell. Sources: hmdb.org's Florida Dept of State historical marker (F-716, erected 2011) + floridastateparks.org.
- Dr. James F. Sistrunk (civil-rights-leaders-james-sistrunk) -- Broward's first Black physician, co-founded Provident Hospital with Mizell (1938). Sources: floridacivilrightsmuseum.org + Westside Gazette. NOTE: sources disagree on exact birth/death years (1891-1966 per Westside Gazette/LocalWiki/FindAGrave vs 1897-1967 per Florida Civil Rights Museum) -- summary omits specific years, personReview basis records the discrepancy.
- Dr. Calvin H. Shirley (civil-rights-leaders-calvin-shirley) -- one of 4 Black physicians who sued to integrate Broward General Hospital's staff. Sources: floridastateparks.org + Westside Gazette obituary (both agree died 2012 age 91).
- W. George Allen (civil-rights-leaders-w-george-allen) -- first Black UF law grad (1962), led Broward school integration lawsuits, first Black president of a major FL bar assoc (1988). Sources: news.ufl.edu (auto reputable_secondary via .edu) + WLRN Public Media (both reported his Nov 2019 death same week).

All 4 cleared the incremental-publish gate at conf=0.765 (2 reputable_secondary lineages, same formula/threshold as Mizell and the earlier HOF/Divine Nine batch). personReview markers set on this session's explicit direction ("find more names" / prior "let's get him added"), basis = each figure's death independently confirmed by 2 sources, decades-deceased in every case.

Two more host reviews added to REPUTABLE_SECONDARY_HOST_SUFFIXES (packages/ops-data/scripts/lib/tier1-sources.ts): thewestsidegazette.com (Broward's oldest Black-owned newspaper, since 1971) and wlrn.org (South Florida's NPR/PBS member station). Pushed to staging (green), not yet promoted to main.

Skipped for insufficient sourcing: Alphonso Giles (1922-2015, ferried Black residents to the segregated beach by boat) -- only found on floridastateparks.org, no independent second source located. Also not pursued: George & Agnes Burrows, Leona Collins/Sylvia Aldridge (conflicting accounts of who the third Provident Hospital co-founder was -- Florida Civil Rights Museum says Leona Collins, CBS Miami says Sylvia Aldridge; needs resolution before staging either name).

Lane total so far: 5 people (Mizell + these 4), all from one hub page. Broader roster-building (other counties/states) remains open.

comments.author: Gerald Dagher
comments.text:
2026-07-29: expanded beyond Florida -- first two out-of-state names, both live in bb_canonical.entities:

- Nathan Francis Mossell (civil-rights-leaders-nathan-mossell), Philadelphia, PA -- first African American to earn a UPenn medical degree (1882), founded the Frederick Douglass Memorial Hospital (1895), founding member of the Niagara Movement and Philadelphia's NAACP branch (1910). Sources: archives.upenn.edu + exhibits.temple.edu -- two independent .edu institutions, no allowlist change needed (the confidence engine already treats .edu as reputable_secondary by rule, conservatively). conf=0.765.
- William F. Penn (civil-rights-leaders-william-f-penn), Atlanta, GA -- first African American to graduate Yale Medical School (1897), founding officer of the Atlanta NAACP branch (1917), founded the Fair Haven Infirmary. Sources: onlineexhibits.library.yale.edu (.edu) + a 1917 Library of Congress photograph (loc.gov, NAACP Records collection) naming him by name as a branch officer -- loc.gov is TIER1/government_record tier, which is why this one scored conf=0.790, the highest in the lane so far.

No new code changes this round -- both people cleared the gate using hosts already covered by existing rules (.edu auto-reputable_secondary, .gov auto-government_record), unlike the Florida batches which needed REPUTABLE_SECONDARY_HOST_SUFFIXES additions.

Skipped: a "John Brown" physician who founded the Pittsburgh NAACP (per a 2022 Virginia DHR historical marker, "An African American Family of Doctors," Winchester VA -- hmdb.org m=273845, siblings Sara/Edward/Harrison/Nancy/James Brown also notable). Did not stage -- "John Brown" is too common a name to safely find a second source without real risk of conflating him with an unrelated person, same class of error as the earlier Bill Foster/Glover School false-positive incidents. Would need his full name/middle initial from a primary source before this is safe to pursue.

Lane total: 7 people across 3 states (FL x5, PA x1, GA x1). Method now proven repeatable outside Florida -- university archives (.edu) and LOC photo collections (.gov) are turning out to be reliable low-friction source pairs for historical (pre-1970s) figures nationally, better than relying on state-park-style hub pages which only exist for Florida so far.

title: Lane C: agent fleet for enrichment + verification (Haiku fan-out, Sonnet adjudication)
description:
Agents enrich and verify a FIXED input roster from Lane B. They do NOT discover entities by open-ended search -- that is the mechanism that produced the BJS fabrication and the banned-books records removed in 98f7803d.

DESIGN:
- Haiku, parallel, strict JSON schema: one roster row in, one normalized entity record out (display_name, kind, dates, location, identifiers, primary source URL). Narrow, low-judgment, high-volume. Cheapest tier that can do this reliably.
- Sonnet, single pass, only on rows Haiku flags thin/ambiguous, plus name-collision adjudication against existing 1395 canonical entities.
- NO agent has database write access. Output -> JSON fixture -> schema validation -> human/automated gate -> repo-glwv promoter.
- Reject any record whose source URL does not resolve or does not mention the subject.

COST SHAPE: bounded by roster size (~450 rows), not by open-ended search depth. One Haiku call per row, Sonnet only on the flagged minority.

title: Redirect bug: /stories/:path* and /themes/:path* catch-alls destroy slug, dead-end published URLs at generic /chapters
description:
apps/web/next.config.* redirects() has:
  { source: '/stories/:path*', destination: '/chapters', permanent: true }
  { source: '/themes/:path*', destination: '/chapters', permanent: true }
Both catch-alls drop the matched path segment entirely — every specific story/theme
URL 308s to the generic /chapters index, not to its equivalent chapter. Confirmed live
locally: /stories/after-the-second-reconstruction -> /chapters (302/308, loses slug);
/themes/redlining -> /chapters (same). This is a real content-loss/dead-link regression:
externally linked or indexed URLs for at least 5 published stories (after-the-second-reconstruction,
before-the-battle-cry, the-log-cabin-costume, +2 more per story-groups.ts) and 6 theme_ids
(redlining, wealth_gap, drug_policy_state, environmental_racism, urban_renewal, voting_rights)
now permanently redirect to a page that doesn't mention their content.

Also affects apps/web/src/lib/theme-impact/source.ts entityCrossReferenceHref(), which still
generates /themes/{themeId}#chapter-N, /stories/{slug}, and /themes/{themeId}/questions/{questionId}
hrefs for entity-page cross-references — these now silently degrade to the generic chapters index
via the same catch-all, losing the specific target entirely (not a crash, but wrong destination).

Root fix needs two mappings that don't fully exist yet:
1. themeId -> chapter slug, only 2 of 6 exist today (redlining -> buying-a-home,
   wealth_gap -> the-gap-that-never-closed via packages/ops-data/fixtures/articles/*.ts).
   The other 4 theme_ids have no authored chapter (blocked on repo-8602).
2. storySlug -> chapter anchor for "unbound" stories that never got folded into a theme
   chapter (see story-groups.ts 'Standalone' grouping) — no such mapping exists.

Until repo-8602 lands the remaining chapters, the catch-all redirect can't correctly
resolve all cases; a themeId/storySlug -> chapter-slug lookup with a sensible default
(index, as today) for unmapped ids is the right shape, not a guess made under this bead.
notes: 2026-07-29 route retirement update: stories are deleted (repo-dx4n/repo-8dj0 closed), so the storySlug->chapter-anchor mapping half of this bug is MOOT — there are no story URLs left to preserve beyond the redirects, and entity-page cross-references now resolve packet-only via THEME_CHAPTER_SLUGS (verified live: Bronzeville 'Appears in' -> /chapters/buying-a-home). Remaining scope is ONLY the 4 theme_ids without authored chapters (environmental_racism, urban_renewal, drug_policy_state, voting_rights) whose /themes/:path* redirects land on the generic /chapters index — still blocked on repo-ewoj/repo-8602 chapter authoring.

title: [bug] Discovery campaigns cron fails hourly on main: kill-switch skip exits 1

title: Evidence capture mandate + backfill: snapshot every cited source (anti-rot, anti-spoof)
description:

Meanwhile link rot is a certainty (~5%/yr) and captures are the single control that simultaneously mitigates rot, drift, and after-the-fact spoofing disputes (we can prove what the source said when we cited it). The fetch layer already exists and is safe (executeSafeFetch, packages/security/src/url-safety/); research-intake already PLANS capture ('not wired yet' per docs/research/research-operations.md).

DESIGN (Haiku/Sonnet-executable):
1. Wire capture into runResearchIntake (packages/operator-cli/src/research-intake.ts + intake.ts): after runQuickAddFetch succeeds, persist bytes-hash + snapshot to storage, insert source_captures + retrieval_events. Reuse buildCitationPrefill metadata.
2. New verb capture-backfill in packages/operator-cli/src/cli.ts following research-operations.md conventions (JSON out, --commit gated, --max-captures budget flag). Input surfaces: bb_public.release_entities (citation URLs inside claims jsonb), bb_reference.theme_impact_packets observations[].provenance.sourceUrl, bb_reference.articles references. Dedupe by normalized URL before fetching.
3. Wayback: POST to SPN2 (web.archive.org/save) when keys available; store returned snapshot URL in source_captures metadata. Absent keys => log and continue; capture locally regardless.
4. Storage: follow whatever store source_captures rows already use for their 14 rows (inspect before inventing); if none, smallest viable is a captures/ prefix in the project's Supabase storage bucket with sha256-named objects.
Entity-scope note (owner directive): this mandate covers ENTITY claim evidence, not just chapters — the entire harness.
acceptance_criteria: 1) research-intake's planSelectiveCapture step is wired: a committed intake produces a bb_evidence.source_captures row (sha256 of retrieved bytes, storage ref, retrieval_events entry) — no longer a no-op note. 2) A backfill lane (operator-cli verb, safe-by-default --commit pattern) walks cited URLs from: release_entities claims' citations, theme packet observation sourceUrls, article references — and captures each reachable one; unreachable ones get a retrieval_events failure row + Wayback lookup fallback. 3) Wayback SPN2 secondary anchoring behind a flag (archive.org keys via 1Password / docs/research/agent-local-env.md if present; skip gracefully if absent). 4) Coverage report: capture rate per surface (entities/packets/articles) printed by the lane; target stated in report, not hardcoded. 5) Rate-limited and robots-respecting via the existing BB-030 safe-fetch path — no raw fetch calls.

title: Harness-wide source integrity policy: tier registry, DOI resolution, corroboration rule
description:
WHY (2026-07-26 deep audit): the adapter layer validates shape/volume/drift (contract.ts, gates.ts, drift.ts, run-health.ts) but nothing validates content AUTHENTICITY or source QUALITY. Threat ranking for this project, weighed deliberately: 1. self-fabrication by our own agents (has happened twice: BJS near-miss, placeholder contentHashes) — highest frequency; 2. link rot / content drift — certainty over time; 3. AI-slop laundering (fake papers, citation mills, SEO farms misquoting real studies) — the SearXNG+local-LLM overnight lanes are precisely where this enters; 4. targeted spoofing/sabotage — low probability today, asymmetric damage; transport layer already covered by BB-030 SSRF-safe fetch + DNS pinning. This bead addresses 3+4 cheaply and closes the citation half of 1. Deliberately NOT in scope (overkill now): content signing, notarization, multi-region fetch comparison.

DESIGN (Sonnet-executable):
1. Tier registry: packages/domain/src/provenance/source-tiers.ts. T1 = official statistical agencies (census.gov, bjs.ojp.gov, bls.gov, cdc.gov, ussc.gov, fed sites) + peer-reviewed journals (doi-resolvable, journal in a maintained allowlist). T2 = NBER/Fed working papers, university presses, .edu research centers, national archives (nara, loc, si.edu). T3 = established nonprofits/journalism with named methodology (Vera, Sentencing Project, Eviction Lab, Brennan Center, ProPublica). T4 = everything else. Data shape: domain-pattern -> tier + rationale; export lookupSourceTier(url).
2. DOI resolution check: small client for api.crossref.org/works/{doi} (fallback api.openalex.org/works/doi:{doi}); both free, no key. Compare normalized title (case/punct-insensitive), first-author surname, venue. New validate step in packages/ops-data/scripts/articles.ts and theme-packets.ts for references carrying doi; also callable from the enrichment judge bridge (packages/operator-cli/src, runEnrichmentJudge path).
3. Corroboration rule: extend packet/article schema with anchors[] per load-bearing figure; validate checks presence + tier of anchors. Enforcement of the two-anchor rule is a validate error for status='published', warning for 'review'.
4. Enrichment tier-tagging: where SearXNG results enter the judge (operator-cli enrichment lanes), attach tier to each source snippet; judge prompt template updated to weight/discard T4.
Wire-in points must reuse assertEvidenceSourceValid in packages/domain/src/provenance/source.ts rather than adding a parallel checker.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A source-tier registry module exists in packages/domain/src/provenance/ and is consulted by adapter gates and the enrichment judge bridge. 2) Any scholarly citation (packet reference, article reference, or enrichment-produced claim citing a paper) fails validation unless its DOI resolves via Crossref/OpenAlex and returned title+authors+venue match the stored citation. 3) Load-bearing figures (rendered in stat/figure/pullquote blocks) declare two independent T1/T2 anchors or one T1 anchor + replication-package verification; validate enforces the declaration's presence. 4) SearXNG-sourced content in enrichment lanes is tier-tagged before reaching judge models; T4 content cannot create or modify claims without a T1-T3 corroborating source. 5) Applies to entity claims (bb_canonical) and packets/articles alike — one policy module, not per-surface copies.
notes: Status: criteria 1,3,4,5 fully landed; criterion 2 landed for article references and packet artifacts (gateDoiCitations, CHECK_DOIS=1) but not yet for enrichment-produced entity claims (bb_canonical) — editorial claims only carry citationHref today, no doi/title/author/venue fields. Tracked as repo-yj2q. Sub-beads: repo-ljv0 (closed), repo-vqsz (closed), repo-ujme (closed), repo-vdtm (closed), repo-xjxf (closed), repo-yj2q (open, follow-up). Leaving this parent open until repo-yj2q lands so criterion 2 is fully satisfied per the bead's own acceptance text.
close_reason: All 5 criteria now satisfied: (1) source-tier registry landed; (2) DOI resolution now covers all three citation surfaces -- article references, theme-impact packet artifacts, and editorial/entity claims (repo-yj2q closed this last gap for bb_canonical claims); (3) two-anchor corroboration rule landed; (4) SearXNG enrichment tier-tagging landed; (5) one shared policy module (lookupSourceTier/checkDoiCitation in @repo/domain) consulted by every surface, no per-surface copies. Sub-beads repo-ljv0/vqsz/ujme/vdtm/xjxf/yj2q all closed.

title: Test harness gap: validate gates never touch sources — add provenance verification + research-artifact requirements
description: Confirmed 2026-07-26: articles.ts validate and theme-packets.ts validate are offline shape + inline-citation-integrity checks only. Nothing in the harness (a) fetches any sourceUrl, (b) checks a cited figure against its source, (c) requires evidence that a literature or counter-literature search was performed, or (d) verifies contentHash is a real hash of source content. Smoking gun: wealth-gap-packets.ts OBS.incomeBlack1972.contentHash = 'eyJtZXJpY0kn-style truncated base64 placeholder and OBS.incomeWhite1972.contentHash is literally its own spine-id string — both pass validate. The contentHash comparison in theme-packets.ts:237 only compares packet vs DB canonical row, i.e. internal consistency, not external truth. Proposed additions: (1) validate --provenance mode that fetches each sourceUrl (or a cached snapshot) and fails on 404/placeholder hashes; (2) require a researchLog artifact per packet (queries run, papers found incl. strongest counter-paper, figures cross-checked) checked by the gate for existence + coverage of every observationId; (3) hash discipline: contentHash must be sha256 of a retrievable snapshot stored under a fixtures/snapshots dir so figures are re-verifiable offline. Relates: repo-e9yj (research process), repo-56pb, repo-8602. This closes the class of bug that caused the earlier BJS fabrication — the gate would have caught it.
design:
ARCHITECTURE CORRECTION (2026-07-26 deep audit): the primary fix is DB-BINDING, not URL fetching. bb_reference.statistical_observations (15,039 rows) already holds adapter-ingested, content-hashed values for the exact series the packets hand-retyped: dkks-percapita-wealth-black-nation / dkks-percapita-wealth-white-nation / dkks-wealth-ratio-white-black-nation (full 1860-2020, source 'derenoncourt-wealth-of-two-nations'), SCF net worth (scf-median-net-worth-by-race-1989-2022), Census H-5 income (census-h5-median-hh-income-by-race-1967-2024), homeownership, CPS turnout, BJS admissions, USSC drug sentencing. Curated CSVs live in packages/ops-data/fixtures/reference-indicators/. 15 spine_series rows exist in bb_reference.spine_series.

IMPLEMENTATION (Sonnet-executable):
1. In packages/ops-data/scripts/theme-packets.ts validate: add a db-binding pass. For each packet observation, look up bb_reference.statistical_observations by (metric_id, reference_period, race_ethnicity_slice). If found: estimate must match exactly (or within declared rounding noted in packet metadata); contentHash must equal the DB row's content_hash. If not found: observation must be flagged provenance:'external' and carry a full sourceUrl + retrievedAt; these are the only rows the optional --provenance fetch mode needs to check.
2. Hash-format lint (offline, always on): contentHash must match /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/. This alone catches the two placeholder hashes in wealth-gap-packets.ts lines ~159/~177.
3. researchLog artifact requirement per packet (kept from original scope): machine-checkable list of observationId -> verification path + strongest counter-paper citation (per repo-e9yj).
4. Same pattern for articles: packages/ops-data/scripts/articles.ts validate should verify every stat block value that names a packetId observation against the packet (already partially done) AND transitively against the DB when DATABASE_URL is set.
DO NOT build URL-fetching as the primary gate; fetch is a fallback for the small set of observations with no adapter coverage. New adapters are the durable fix for repeat sources.

title: Sentenced chapter: build on contested-causation footing (Pfaff/Forman vs Alexander) with DisputeBlock
description: Pre-research finding before authoring the drug-policy chapter (repo-8602): this topic has the WEAKEST causal consensus of the four. What is solidly documented: 100:1 crack/powder sentencing disparity (Anti-Drug Abuse Act 1986 — statute is a real artifact), Black crack-offense sentences ~2x white, arrest-rate disparities despite similar usage rates. What is genuinely disputed: how much the drug war drives the racial composition of the prison population — Pfaff's analysis shows releasing all drug-top-charge prisoners moves the Black share of prisons by ~1 point; Forman's 'Locking Up Our Own' complicates the top-down narrative. So the Alexander 'New Jim Crow' framing must NOT be asserted as settled cause. Structure: assert the documented enforcement/sentencing disparities plainly (they're paper-trail facts), use DisputeBlock for the mass-incarceration causal debate, keep prison-population claims juxtaposed. This is the one chapter where the current cautious stance is RIGHT — the fix from repo-e9yj is calibration, not blanket causal assertion. Statute text (ADAA 1986, Fair Sentencing Act 2010 reducing 100:1 to 18:1) = primary documents.

Also added the 1880/1890/1900 DKKS intermediate benchmarks (DB-bound, read-only verified against bb_reference.statistical_observations) to show the convergence-stalled slope instead of jumping 1870->1922. The fixture CSV is packages/ops-data/fixtures/reference-indicators/dkks-wealth-gap-1860-2020.csv via the dkks-wealth adapter. Benchmark verification source: DKKS QJE 2024 replication archive — Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/H6NXUH and openICPSR project 194203 (also elloraderenoncourt.com/us-inequality-data). Use the intermediate decades (1880: 19.0, 1890: 14.9, 1900: 11.4 ratios, already in DB) to strengthen the 'convergence stalled' arc instead of jumping 1870->1922. Mechanism observations (Freedman's Bank collapse 1874, SSA 1935 ag/domestic exclusion, GI Bill local denial) remain new research: ingest via a small adapter or provenance:'external' observations with captures per the capture-mandate bead.

title: Research harness: per-claim causal calibration + counter-literature pass
description: Learning from wealth-gap chapter review (2026-07-26). Two gaps in the current research harness: (1) method_stance is a single packet-level switch (e.g. 'juxtaposition'), forcing the weakest framing onto every claim, even ones where the economics literature asserts cause with strong identification (VRA turnout/wage effects, HOLC boundary effects). Change the approach so causal confidence is calibrated per claim, in three tiers: ASSERT (peer-reviewed causal identification exists — cite the study inline, state cause plainly), MECHANISM (documented policy exclusion with paper trail — Freedman's Bank, SSA/GI Bill exclusions — name the mechanism without econometric hedging), JUXTAPOSE (co-movement only — keep current stance). (2) The harness researches supporting evidence but never runs a counter-literature pass. Redlining example: Fishback/Rose/Snowden 2022 (NBER w29244, JUE) shows HOLC lent to Black homeowners ~proportionately and FHA did the redlining independently of HOLC maps — this materially affects how the HOLC map should be framed in buying-a-home. Add a mandatory 'strongest revisionist/counter paper' search step to packet research, and route genuine disputes into DisputeBlock (component already exists) instead of silently choosing a side. Acceptance: written guidance in docs/content/ (extend era-immersion-style.md or sibling doc) + packet schema supports per-observation stance.
notes: DEEP-AUDIT ADDENDUM (2026-07-26): schema support already exists — bb_reference.theme_impact_packets has a causal_claim_ids column (currently unused). Wire the per-claim tiers there: each ASSERT/MECHANISM/JUXTAPOSE designation becomes a causal-claim record id rather than prose in method_note. Standard of evidence for ASSERT tier: a peer-reviewed causal paper WITH a retrievable replication package verified per the replication-verification bead (AHM openICPSR 127803 is the model case). Counter-literature pass is mandatory for ASSERT and MECHANISM tiers and gets recorded in the packet researchLog artifact (repo-t6up).

title: Author remaining 2 flagship chapters (Sentenced, Casting a ballot)
description:
Two of the four planned flagship chapters are DELIVERED and live: buying-a-home (redlining, commit 97e71183, 4,399 prose words) and the-gap-that-never-closed (wealth_gap, commit fdbf0d72). Both audit 'ok'.

REMAINING: Sentenced (drug_policy_state, packet sentenced-drug-policy-packet.ts) and Casting a ballot (voting_rights, packet voting-rights-packets.ts). Both packets are published and audit 'ok', so the data floor is already in place — the work is authoring.

The bar has moved since this issue was written. The two delivered chapters set the standard the remaining two must meet, and it is enforced by gates, not convention:
- gateProseWordFloor: MIN_PUBLISHED_PROSE_WORDS = 2000. Both delivered chapters cleared it with room (4,399 and similar).
- docs/methodology/chapter-fact-validation.md 3-layer protocol: research pass -> independent refute pass that re-fetches every URL -> gate run. The refute pass is not optional; on buying-a-home it caught a corrupted verbatim SCOTUS quote and a causation error that had already survived the first pass.
- docs/content/era-immersion-style.md: forward-chronological era sections, second person, no rewind. Each era must show a rule operating on a NAMED household, not just narrate the rule.
- Source tiers: T4 hard-errors on published. Prefer .gov/.edu primaries. SCOTUS verbatim quotes MUST come from tile.loc.gov US Reports PDFs — Cornell LII transcriptions carry OCR corruption.
- Observations are field-by-field verified against canonical bb_reference.statistical_observations rows; new numbers enter as [ref:] citations, never invented stat blocks.

Per repo-k7su, Sentenced additionally requires a DisputeBlock for the mass-incarceration causal debate — that chapter has the weakest causal consensus of the four and must NOT assert the Alexander framing as settled.

Each chapter is a full session: research agents -> refute verifiers -> validate/apply/promote/project -> browser QA. Do not attempt both in one session.

title: SUSPECT: census income/poverty fixtures (repo-zxjz.3) smoothed + heavily rounded
description:
Validation during repo-zxjz.11 found the census historical income/poverty fixtures show fabrication/smoothing fingerprints. Endpoints are roughly plausible but values are untrustworthy for a data-forward flagship. Verify against real Census sources before splicing; re-ingest the affected years.

## Evidence
- census-p2-poverty-rate-black-nation: recent years step perfectly linearly — 2021=18.5, 2022=18.0, 2023=17.5, 2024=17.0 (+/-0.5/yr). Real values differ (Census: 2021 Black ~19.5%, 2022 ~17.1%, 2023 ~17.8%) and are not monotone. Older years (2015-2020) look irregular/real; the recent tail looks extrapolated.
- census-h5-median-hh-income-black-nation: everything rounded to nearest $500-$1000 (56000, 56500, 57000, 40000, 33000, 28000). Recent tail declines by exactly $500/yr (2022=57000, 2023=56500, 2024=56000). Real Census H-5 values are not round (e.g. $52,860). Magnitudes plausible, precision fake.

## Required fix
- Re-ingest from real sources: H-5 (https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cps/tables/time-series/historical-income-households/h05.xlsx) and hstpov2 (https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cps/tables/time-series/historical-poverty-people/hstpov2.xlsx), using published annual values (unrounded), gaps left as gaps.
- Spot-check 3 years/series against the xlsx; replace the fixtures; re-apply.

## Impact
Feeds disparity context across themes; lower severity than repo-ypfp (BJS) because it is not the sole backbone of a flagship, but must not ship as-is.

## Also verified GOOD in the same pass (no action needed)
- DKKS wealth ratio (repo-zxjz.2): authentic irregular benchmark years — EXCEPT 1929 computes ratio=0.0 (missing white per-capita value stored as 0). Small fix: store as null/omit rather than 0.
- NCHS life expectancy (repo-zxjz.5): real, includes 2015-17 dip + 2020-21 COVID collapse; honest nonwhite/colored/Black RaceLabel seam column.
- Homeownership decennial 1900-2000 + ACS 2005-2024 (repo-zxjz.6): real, well-sourced, matches published rates.
- HMDA denial rates (repo-zxjz.7): real, sourced from FFIEC aggregations.
- CPS turnout (repo-zxjz.8): real (SHA-256 recorded), BUT coverage is 1980-2020 only — pre-1980 presidential years (1964/68/72/76) and 2024 are missing despite the "1964-2024" bead title. File/track as a coverage gap, not fabrication.
close_reason: Re-ingested real, source-verified annual Census income/poverty data for both races; typecheck clean.

comments.author: Gerald Dagher

(source table has no NH-specific series before 1972 -- 1983 also missing/N in source, left

title: 5 spine-series ingestion scripts fail against current DB schema
description:
Merged spine-series-phase0 branch (commit f98b69bf on staging) landed 7 ingestion scripts written earlier against an older bb_reference schema. Migration 20260725000000_spine_series.sql applied cleanly (spine_series/spine_segments/spine_observations_v now exist). BJS CSAT + admissions scripts applied successfully (154 obs total, existing metric series already present). 5 scripts fail:

- ingest-national-hmda-aggregates.ts: FK violation on statistical_observations.metric_id — statistical_series rows for hmda-denial-rate-* not created/matched before insert.
- ingest-national-homeownership.ts: same FK violation pattern (acs-homeownership-rate-*, census-decennial-homeownership-*).
- ingest-nchs-life-expectancy.ts: statistical_series insert violates estimate_type check constraint — script's estimate_type value not in current allowed set.
- ingest-phase1-cps-a1.ts: same estimate_type check constraint violation.
- ingest-phase2-census-historical-income.ts: statistical_observations.boundary_version NOT NULL violation — script doesn't populate boundary_version, current schema requires it.

Also: ingest-phase2-bls-unemployment.ts hit a BLS API daily rate-limit on its registered key (not a schema issue) — retry after limit resets, or use a different key.

Dry-runs for all 5 (minus BLS) look correct (observation counts, sanity checks matched bead acceptance criteria) — this is purely an apply-time schema drift issue between when these scripts were authored and the current statistical_series/statistical_observations DDL. Fix: inspect current column list + constraints (estimate_type allowed values, boundary_version requirement, series-must-exist-before-observations ordering) and align each script's series-creation step accordingly.

Blocks repo-zxjz.11 (splice assembly) same as the parent ingestion issues.
notes:

- ingest-nchs-life-expectancy.ts: estimate_type 'estimate' violated the CHECK constraint; changed to 'mean'. Also fixed jurisdiction_id 'nation:united-states' -> 'nation:US' (FK violation once estimate_type was fixed). Applied: 38 observations.
- ingest-phase1-cps-a1.ts: estimateType 'reported' and periodType 'presidential-election-year' both violated CHECK constraints; changed to 'percentage' and 'custom-range'. Applied: 41 observations.
- ingest-phase2-census-historical-income.ts: boundary_version was hardcoded null (NOT NULL violation); added constant 'nation-2024' following the SCF wealth / BJS CSAT vintage convention. Applied: 84 observations (20 income black + 20 income white-nh + 22 poverty black + 22 poverty white-nh).

Total applied across all 5 scripts: 244 observations. pnpm --filter @repo/ops-data typecheck and pnpm --filter @repo/domain typecheck both pass. Committed as 4a2baa40 on staging, not pushed. Left in_progress per instructions -- ingest-phase2-bls-unemployment.ts (BLS rate limit, out of scope) still needs a retry after the limit resets before this bead can close.

title: CI: Discovery campaigns workflow reports failure on benign kill-switch skip
description:
The 'Discovery campaigns' GHA workflow (.github/workflows/discovery-campaigns.yml) fails every scheduled run (hourly for discovery-campaign-rss) instead of succeeding when the campaign is intentionally skipped.

Root cause (two compounding issues):
1. No DATABASE_URL secret is configured for this workflow, so the kill-switch check (scripts/check-kill-switch.mjs) fails closed and reports state=engaged (this fail-closed behavior is correct/intentional).
2. discovery-dispatch (packages/operator-cli/src/bin.ts) exits with code 1 when the result is skipped_kill_switch, treating a benign, expected skip as a hard failure. Its own JSON summary even calls it a 'message', not an error.

This has produced 7 straight failed runs in the last 7 hours (all discovery-campaign-rss cron), pure CI noise for expected behavior.

Fix (either clears it, ideally both):
- Add DATABASE_URL secret for this workflow so the kill switch can be read for real, and/or
- Make discovery-dispatch exit 0 (not 1) on skipped_kill_switch, since it's a no-op outcome, not an error.

Distinct from repo-y9ef (Build/Typecheck lane DATABASE_URL) — that's a different workflow.

## Context
Found while investigating why blackstory.app production kept serving stale content; GHA failures were noticed as a side finding, unrelated to the Vercel deploy issue.
close_reason: Fixed: added Postgres service to discovery-campaigns.yml (same pattern as ci.yml's integration-postgres job) so the kill switch can be read for real, and changed discovery-dispatch to only exit non-zero on status: 'error', not the benign skipped_kill_switch.

STYLE CHECKLIST (docs/content/era-immersion-style.md)
- [x] Second person, present tense inside every era; tense shifts only at jump-cuts.
- [x] Five-part era shape x4 eras + present-day close handing off to the chart.
- [x] Rule-in-force = verbatim primary-doc quotes, cited (literacy test, VRA 4(c)/5).

- [x] No em dashes (grep 0). No internal tracker/bead ids, no "the user", no config paths in packet content.

GAPS / DIVERGENCES FROM ISSUE ASSUMPTIONS
1. Turnout spine range is 1980-2020, NOT the issue's assumed 1964-2024. spine-turnout-black-us / -white-us cover presidential years 1980-2020 only (both spine_series.status=review); 1964/68/72/76 and 2024 are not ingested (spine_series.comparability_note points at repo-zxjz.8). The CPS-universe discussion lives ONLY in method_note, never in body prose. If a genuine VAP->CVAP seam needs to exist, that is a spine ingestion gap (repo-zxjz.8), not something to fabricate here.

I cited the live canonical row hash. Not blocking; worth reconciling at the epic number audit.

title: Era-immersion writing style guide

title: Splice: assemble 8 national spine series with seam checks
description:
Assemble the 8 national spine series from Phase 1 metrics. This is judgment work: seam choice, overlap validation, comparability notes.

## Spines to build (spine_id / segments, priority = later source wins overlaps unless noted)
1. spine-wealth-ratio-white-black-us: dkks-wealth-ratio (1860–2020) + SCF-derived ratio (1989–2022, compute from existing scf-median-wealth metrics as derived_measurements first). Note: DKKS is per-capita mean, SCF is household median — the note must say the two measure DIFFERENT gaps; consider publishing as two overlaid segments rather than a hard splice (allowed: seam type "overlay").
2. spine-median-hh-income-black-us + white-nh twin (census H-5, single source, 1967–present; single-segment spine is fine, justify in comparability_note).
3. spine-poverty-rate-black-us (+ white-nh twin) (census table 2, 1959–present).
4. spine-unemployment-rate-black-us (+ white twin): BLS 1972–present; optional pre-1972 decennial census unemployment as context segment only if trivially available — otherwise skip.
5. spine-life-expectancy-black-us (+ white twin): NCHS 1900–present; seam where "nonwhite"->"Black" labeling changes (~1970) documented with both-year values.
6. spine-homeownership-black-us (+ white twin): decennial 1900–2000 (priority 2) + ACS annual 2005–2024 (priority 1); seam check at 2000 vs 2005–06.
7. spine-imprisonment-rate-black-us (+ white twin): BJS/CSAT 1978–2023.
8. spine-turnout-black-us (+ white twin): CPS A-1 1964–2020/24, with the universe change (VAP -> CVAP) recorded as an in-series seam.

## Method requirements
- For every seam with overlapping years: compute pct difference at overlap, store in spine_segments.seam_check, and flag any seam with >10% divergence for review (comment on issue) rather than silently splicing.
- Every ratio/gap displayed to users must exist as a derived_measurements row (formula field filled) or a spine — never computed ad hoc downstream.
- Register each spine's disparity companion (black-minus-white or ratio) as derived_measurements referencing input obs ids.

## Acceptance
- 8 spine_series rows status `review`, each drawing correctly from spine_observations_v (spot-check 3 years per spine against raw obs).
- Seam report posted as issue comment: every seam, overlap values, divergence, decision.
