title: Schema: spine_series + spine_segments + spine_observations_v
description:
Create migration `supabase/migrations/<ts>_spine_series.sql` (follow style of `20260721220000_statistical_series_observations.sql`, including RLS/select policies matching `20260723204100_consolidate_bb_reference_select_policies.sql`).

## Tables
`bb_reference.spine_series`
- spine_id text PK (e.g. `spine-homeownership-rate-black-us`)
- title text, outcome text, race_ethnicity_slice text, geography_type text default 'nation'
- unit text, definition text NOT NULL (the harmonized concept, e.g. "share of households owner-occupied, Black householder")
- comparability_note text NOT NULL (global caveats across the whole spine)
- theme text, status text default 'draft' check (draft|review|published)
- created_at/updated_at timestamptz

`bb_reference.spine_segments`
- id text PK (`seg:<spine_id>:<start>-<end>`)
- spine_id FK -> spine_series
- metric_id FK -> statistical_series(metric_id)
- period_start text, period_end text (inclusive year strings)
- priority int (when two segments overlap a year, lower number wins)
- splice_note text NOT NULL (what changes at this seam: universe, survey, definition)
- seam_check jsonb (populated by repo-XX-splice QA: overlapping-year values from both sources + pct difference)

## View
`bb_reference.spine_observations_v`: one row per (spine_id, reference_period) resolving each year to the winning segment's observation — join spine_segments -> statistical_observations on metric_id, filter reference_period between period_start/period_end, pick min(priority) per year. Expose: spine_id, reference_period, estimate, unit, source metric_id, source, source_url, splice_note.

## Acceptance
- Migration applies cleanly to a Supabase branch AND locally; typegen (`generate_typescript_types`) run and committed if the repo stores generated types.

title: EPIC: Spine series + era-immersion themes (multi-source patched data storytelling)
description:
## Goal
Turn bb_reference from a pile of recent cross-sections into a story-telling engine: (1) long, multi-source "spine" time series per outcome (Black/white, national, longest possible span) where WE do the patching across sources, and (2) rewritten theme packets in a second-person era-immersion style ("You apply for a mortgage in 1955 / 1985 / 2023") that pair a primary document (the rule in force) with the measured odds from a spine series at each era.

Comparable product: EPI "Racial and ethnic disparities in the United States" chartbook — but with era-spliced series and narrative immersion instead of chart-plus-commentary.

## Non-negotiable principles (apply to every child issue)
1. Users never patch data together. Multi-source stitching happens in our schema (spine_series/spine_segments), with the seam documented, never in the UI or the reader's head.
2. Story-first ingestion: every new dataset/slice ingested must be bound to a spine series or theme packet in the same phase. No speculative breadth loads.
3. Provenance discipline: every observation row carries source, source_url, content_hash, retrieved_at; follow existing row conventions exactly:
   - obs id: `obs:<metric_id>:nation:US:<year>`; jurisdiction_id `nation:US`; status `observed`; race_ethnicity_slice lowercase (`black`, `white`, `white-non-hispanic`, `hispanic`, `all`).
   - Every new metric gets a `bb_reference.statistical_series` row FIRST (metric_id, metric_definition, universe, unit, source_dataset, source_table, source_variable, geography_type, estimate_type, period_type, theme).
4. Never fabricate a data point. If a source year is missing, it stays missing (spine segments may have gaps). If a spot-check value in an issue disagrees with the downloaded source, TRUST THE SOURCE, note the discrepancy in the issue, and continue.
5. Causal claims stay gated: method_stance `juxtaposition` by default; `gated_causal_claim` only when backed by published causal literature cited in the packet (e.g., Aaronson/Hartley/Mazumder 2021 for HOLC).
6. Ingestion mechanism: copy the pattern in `packages/firebase/scripts/ingest-phase1-scf-wealth.ts` (nation-level template) or `ingest-phase1-acs.ts` (API-pull template). New scripts named `ingest-phase2-<source>.ts` in the same directory. Idempotent upserts keyed on obs id.

## Model routing
- Issues labeled `model:haiku`: mechanical ingestion — exact sources, columns, and acceptance checks are specified; no judgment calls. If a source URL is dead or the file layout does not match the issue, STOP and comment on the issue rather than improvising.
- Issues labeled `model:sonnet`: schema design, splicing judgment, document curation, and all writing.

## Phases and dependency order
- Phase 0: schema (spine tables) — blocks Phase 2.
- Phase 1: ingestion backfills (parallel, haiku) + wiring existing loaded data.
- Phase 2: splice assembly — 8 national spine series (sonnet).
- Phase 3: primary-document evidence ingestion (haiku fetch, sonnet curation).
- Phase 4: style guide, then 4 rewritten theme packets (sonnet), then QA/publish gate.

## Definition of done (epic)
- 8 spine series drawable end-to-end from one view each, with documented seams; each has >= 2 source segments or an explicit single-source justification.
- 4 theme packets published in era-immersion style, each binding >= 1 spine series and >= 1 primary document, all sentences claim-linked per existing bb_research conventions.
- No empty-shell artifacts remain in scope: `oa-incarceration-outcome-black-tract` populated; decision recorded (use or drop) for banned_books, census_county_historical_decades.

title: [bug] Entity page dark theme: large blank black block appears mid-page, nav seems to float mid-scroll
description:
Reported by user with a screenshot showing a large solid-black empty area on an entity detail page below the location map section (dark theme). Reproduced live on /entity/lynching_demon_lowman_aiken_vicinity_south_carolina (any entity using the placeholder photo mark -- .ds-entity-photo--mark / .ds-entity-mark -- likely reproduces this; this entity has no real photo, just the fallback 'arch' mark graphic).

Repro steps:
1. Open /entity/lynching_demon_lowman_aiken_vicinity_south_carolina (or another entity lacking a real photo) at desktop width (1440x900).
2. Switch to dark theme (button aria-label 'Switch to dark theme').
3. Scroll down ~600px.
4. Observe: a large solid black/near-black rectangular area occupies roughly the top ~685px of the viewport with no visible content, and the site's nav bar appears to sit mid-viewport below that black area, rather than at the very top (pinned/sticky) or scrolled fully away with the rest of the page -- looks like the nav duplicated or the intro panel above it is oversized.

Investigation so far (not conclusive, needs a fresh thorough pass):
- The entity's intro article panel (.ds-entity-edition__panel--intr, dark bg rgb(28,27,24)) contains a .ds-entity-photo--mark figure that's ~463px tall (516x463), itself made of a .ds-entity-mark placeholder graphic (516x434) plus a figcaption credit line (516x21) -- these two roughly account for the figure's own height, so the figure itself may not be the sole cause.
- Need to determine: (a) is the intro panel/stack unusually tall for entities without a real photo, creating dead space; (b) is the site nav actually duplicating, or is what looks like 'floating mid-page' actually a legitimate in-page 'next/previous record' browsing bar (the page has 'Back to previous record' / 'Next record in list' controls) that's being misread as the global nav; (c) is this specific to dark theme (bg colors blending making an otherwise-normal-but-empty panel read as a jarring 'black block') or a real layout/height bug.
- Check apps/web/src/components/entity/EntityRecordMark.tsx or wherever '.ds-entity-mark' placeholder graphic lives, apps/web/src/app/entity/[id]/EntityEditionSections.tsx (intro panel structure), entity-page.css.

Fix direction: whatever the root cause, the visual result (a large blank dark area with no content, disrupting the page's visual rhythm) is wrong. Verify against multiple entities: one with a real photo (no placeholder mark) and one without, in both light and dark theme, at desktop and mobile widths, to make sure the fix doesn't just move the bug or only fix this one entity.
close_reason: Root cause: .ds-edition-atmosphere-canvas::before / .ds-edition-atmosphere (shared across all v6 edition pages: entity, home, history, stories, methodology, law, about, books, data, themes) used position:fixed for a purely decorative full-viewport background layer, stacked against the site header's own position:fixed layer (z-index 80). This created two competing always-on fixed compositor layers; under some scroll/paint timings the decorative layer failed to repaint and rendered as a large stale solid block over the page -- especially visible in dark theme where the canvas color is near-black. DOM measurements at every scroll depth showed the page's actual layout (panel heights, header position, gaps) was always correct; the defect was a compositing/paint artifact from the redundant fixed layer, not a genuine height/layout bug. Fixed by changing both rules from position:fixed to position:absolute in apps/web/src/components/patterns/edition-atmosphere/edition-atmosphere.css -- every consumer already sets position:relative on its root, so the layer now sizes to the full page content and scrolls with it instead of needing to track the viewport. Verified via DOM getBoundingClientRect + screenshots: entity page without a real photo (lynching_demon_lowman_aiken_vicinity_south_carolina), light+dark theme, desktop (1440x900) and mobile (390x844), at multiple scroll depths -- no dead space, header correctly pinned, panels flow with normal gaps. Typecheck and full web test suite (1031 tests) clean. Could not test an entity WITH a real photo locally (no DATABASE_URL / seed fixtures with primaryImage set), but the changed CSS is shell-level chrome unrelated to which entity media renders, so this does not affect confidence in the fix.

title: [bug] Navbar is too tall (143px) — wordmark's natural aspect ratio inflates the header
description:
User feedback (2026-07-24): 'the navbar is too tall; it feels old.' Measured live: .ds-shell-header renders at 143px. Base header CSS (packages/ui/src/styles/shell-header.css) targets a compact --ds-island-height: 3.5rem (56px) + 0.25rem padding (~64px total), which is a normal modern nav height. But .ds-shell-wordmark__img is sized 'width: 11.5rem; height: auto' -- the lockup PNG's natural aspect ratio computes to ~117px tall at that width, and since the header uses align-items:center with no max-height clamp on children, the wordmark pushes the whole header to 143px instead of the intended ~64px.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT: repo-8ckr (closed earlier today) fixed a DIFFERENT bug where home's navbar logo was inconsistently SMALLER (36px) than every other page (117px) due to a home-only CSS override. That fix was correct -- it removed the override so sizing is now consistent sitewide. Do NOT reintroduce a home-only special case. The real fix here is: the wordmark's shared/base sizing itself needs to be more compact for a navbar context (cap by height instead of by width, e.g. 'height: 2.25rem; width: auto' or similar, so it fits inside a slim ~56-64px bar), applied uniformly in shell-header.css so it stays consistent across ALL pages including home.

Verify the lockup image still meets the 'brand lockup >=168px digital minimum' rule noted in the CSS comment (docs/ui/brand.md) -- check whether that minimum is about on-screen width specifically, or overall size, since shrinking to fit a 56-64px bar height may need reconciling with that documented minimum. If they conflict, flag it rather than silently violating the brand minimum -- may need brand.md's number revisited for navbar context specifically (vs. e.g. footer or marketing placements where the lockup can be larger).

File: packages/ui/src/styles/shell-header.css (.ds-shell-wordmark__img, .ds-shell-wordmark__img--lockup, .ds-shell-header__inner, --ds-island-height token if needed).

Target: header should read as ~56-64px, feel current/compact, and the fix must apply identically across home, explore, history, data, memorial, entity pages (no per-page override).
notes: Fixed: capped .ds-shell-wordmark__img by height (2.25rem) instead of width in packages/ui/src/styles/shell-header.css, applied uniformly (no per-page override) so header renders ~56-70px across all pages instead of 143px. Removed the >=64rem width bump media query since sizing is now height-driven and uniform. Verified live: /explore and /memorial both 56px (light+dark theme), home 70px (pre-existing intentional floating-pill header pattern from apps/web/src/app/shell.css :has(.ds-home-hero) with larger 0.75rem padding + 44px nav-link min-height -- not wordmark-driven, not a regression, not touched). Symbol swap at narrow width (<768px) still works. Typecheck and full web test suite (1021 tests) pass. FLAG: height cap renders the lockup at 64px wide, below brand.md's '168px digital minimum' for the primary lockup. brand.md explicitly addresses this exact scenario: 'Never squeeze the clear space to fit navigation -- reduce the adjacent UI or switch to the symbol alone instead,' which reads as directly applicable to nav, not just marketing placements -- so this is a real documented-constraint conflict, not a false positive. Proceeded with the height-capped lockup per bead brief's explicit fix direction, documented the conflict in a CSS comment above .ds-shell-wordmark__img, but recommend a follow-up decision: either revise brand.md to carve out utility-nav as an exception to the 168px minimum, or switch header to symbol-only at all breakpoints (already done at mobile) to fully honor brand.md as written.

title: Home hero redesign: remove hard seam between map plate and copy background
description:
User feedback with screenshot (2026-07-24): 'The separation between the map and background behind the text is wildly distracting; redesign the hero.' The screenshot shows a hard vertical edge where the hero map plate's brighter basemap meets the darker left half behind the headline/copy -- the hero reads as two glued-together panels instead of one continuous cinematic surface. The map's western half is dimmed behind the copy while the eastern half is bright, with a sharp vertical seam at the boundary.

Design intent (per docs/ui/patterns-cinematic-map.md and the original Pattern D 'map IS the page' concept): the map should read as ONE continuous backdrop across the entire hero, with copy legibility achieved by the CinematicScrim gradient -- not by a hard-edged split. Fix direction: remove the hard vertical boundary; let the basemap render full-bleed across the whole hero panel with a smooth horizontal gradient scrim (dark behind the copy column, fading to clear over the map focus area). The scrim gradient must be gradual enough that no visible seam/edge line exists at any point. Check where the hard edge comes from: could be the copy column's opaque background, a second panel element with its own background, or the map plate not extending under the copy column (hero-map-inset geometry covering only part of the panel). Files: apps/web/src/app/(map)/HeroStage.tsx, map-surfaces.css, shell.css (.ds-home-hero grid), components/patterns/cinematic-map/CinematicScrim.tsx + cinematic-map.css, lib/map-experience/hero-map-inset.ts (verify the plate spans the full panel width -- header comment says it should: 'The plate fills the full rounded hero frame so basemap + pins extend under the copy column; copy sits above a light matte scrim').

Preserve: WCAG-level copy legibility over the map, cinematic Rest/Invite/Engaged behavior, the scroll-away fix from repo-3lzc, CONUS fit from repo-4v3a.4. Verify live with screenshots at desktop width in both themes: no visible vertical seam, headline/copy clearly readable, map pins visible across the full hero including (dimmed) under the copy side.
close_reason: Root cause: .ds-home-hero::before was a flat canvas matte covering only grid column 1 plus a border-right on the copy column -- both ended abruptly at the column boundary, creating the hard vertical seam. Redesign: one continuous canvas-tinted wash spanning the full hero, faded by a 7-stop horizontal mask ramp (opaque behind copy -> transparent over map focus, no visible edge at any point); border seam removed; mobile stacked layout gets a vertical ramp; wash lifts to opacity 0 in Engaged so the full-bleed map is unobstructed. Both themes screenshot-verified at 1440 and 1024: no seam, copy legible, CONUS fully framed, pins visible dimmed under copy. Engage/close verified (state machine + inset restore). Tests 1031 pass; hero-stage.test.ts contracts updated.

title: [bug] /explore: closing an entity card makes ALL entity markers light up/flash
description:
User repro (2026-07-24): on /explore (web), select an entity (record card opens), then close it via the card close button (.ds-nc__close, aria 'Close <name> card'). On close, ALL entity markers on the map appear to light up simultaneously.

Instrumentation from live session narrows the cause: MapLibre layer paint does NOT change across the close (explore-point circle-opacity expression identical before/after, halo 0.16 before/after, explore-point-selected filter ['==',['get','entityId'],''] before AND after -- selection layer paint path is stable). So the flash is NOT canvas-layer paint. Likely culprit: the DOM entity markers (.ds-map-entity-marker maplibregl-marker buttons, e.g. aria 'Clearview', 'P.B.S. Pinchback', 'Switchback School') re-mounting or re-running an entrance/highlight animation when selection state clears -- a React re-render of the marker collection on entitySelected->null would re-trigger any mount animation on every marker at once, reading as 'all entities light up'.

Investigate: how DOM markers are rendered/keyed on /explore (ExploreMapExperience.tsx + MapStage.tsx marker layer / SynchronizedResultList wiring), whether closing the card (dismissing record preview) changes a prop that recreates the marker array identity or clears a CSS class shared by all markers. Fix so closing an entity card changes ONLY the previously-selected marker's visual state; all other markers must be visually untouched (same invariant as repo-4v3a.1/repo-mrmh established for canvas layers -- extend it to the DOM marker path).

Verify live: select entity -> close card -> confirm via DOM observation (MutationObserver on marker class/style changes, or screenshots) that non-selected markers do not re-animate/flash.
close_reason: Root cause: MapStage.syncCircularMarkers rebuilt the entire DOM marker collection (clearMarkers + recreate all ~1373 .ds-map-entity-marker buttons) on every zoomend, and the fixed-pixel discs stayed mounted through the close-camera ease until zoomend — every pin bloomed oversized during the flight then mass-unmounted at once. Canvas paint was stable (as instrumented). Fix: keyed diff by entityId (new src/lib/map-experience/entity-marker-diff.ts, used by syncCircularMarkers — keep/add/remove, in-place idempotent element updates) + gate-clear on the 'zoom' event so discs unmount at the cluster-gate crossing, not zoomend. Verified live both themes via MutationObserver: close now produces 0 marker adds/removes and exactly 1 class change (the previously-selected marker). typecheck + full web test suite pass (1027 tests, new entity-marker-diff.test.ts added).

title: Memorial page: 'Held in the Wall' redesign + wire full 1,680-name dataset
description:
Redesign /memorial per user-approved concept 'Held in the Wall' (merged from idea-set concepts 1+2, approved 2026-07-24):

CONCEPT:
- On load: pure Archive Paper canvas, no header/CTAs/edition panel visible. Empty ~1.5s beat, then names begin fading in slow and sparse (matches existing wall spec restraint, low density, never crowded).
- As it settles into steady cycling rhythm: a 4-line message assembles FROM the names themselves -- each line fades in once (using the same handwriting-face wall mechanic) and, unlike the names around it, STAYS/holds once shown, so by the time all 4 lines have appeared the full message sits fixed and quiet at the center of the field while names keep drifting behind/around it permanently.
- Plays once automatically on load, NOT scroll-gated (so nobody misses it by not scrolling).
- The full readable list link becomes a single small quiet text anchor at the bottom of the viewport, not a card/button -- page should still read as 'blank except for names'.
- Reduced motion: message lines appear immediately in final position (no fade choreography); names render at static low opacity per existing wall spec (memorial-decade-fade.ts / MemorialWallAtmosphere already has this pattern, reuse it).

MESSAGE COPY (drafted + approved, do not rewrite without asking; matches brand.md guardrails -- no em dashes, no completeness overclaims, no lecturing):
  'We say the names because silence is how forgetting starts.'
  'Some of these names you know. Most of them, until now, you didn't.'
  'Every one is a reminder: the fight for equality is not over.'
  'This list will never be finished. That is not a flaw. It is the truth.'

DATA FIX (do regardless, this is the real underlying bug): apps/web/src/components/patterns/memorial-wall/memorial-names.ts currently hardcodes only 64 names. Two much larger verified research datasets already exist and are unused: docs/research/police-violence-memorial-names.json (1104 entries) and docs/research/racial-terror-memorial-names.json (576 entries), totaling 1680. Wire the wall + the full readable list (MemorialSections.tsx via memorialNamesAlphabetical()) to source from these datasets instead of (or merged with, deduped against) the 64-name hardcoded list. Check field shapes/normalization needed (name spelling care per brand.md, handle context/place/year fields per existing MemorialNameEntry type in components/atmosphere/memorial-names.ts which already models a similar shape -- reuse that pattern/normalization logic if applicable rather than re-inventing). Preserve MEMORIAL_NAMES_REQUIRED plate-eligibility logic (isMemorialNamePlateEligible -- names need given+family name to look complete on the wall).

Files: apps/web/src/app/memorial/page.tsx, MemorialSections.tsx, memorial-copy.ts, memorial-edition.css, memorial-panel-chrome.ts; apps/web/src/components/patterns/memorial-wall/MemorialWallAtmosphere.tsx, memorial-names.ts, pack-memorial-names.ts; apps/web/src/lib/map-experience/memorial-decade-fade.ts (reduced-motion pattern reference).

Spec: docs/ui/design-direction-v6-memorial.md (update this doc to reflect the new concept once shipped).
notes:
PERFORMANCE ISSUE FOUND (2026-07-24), do not close until fixed: pack-memorial-names.ts's collision-avoidance packing is O(names x maxAttempts x placedBoxes) -- up to 220 names x 280 attempts x up to 220 growing boxes = potentially millions of overlap checks, run SYNCHRONOUSLY on every mount of MemorialWallAtmosphere AND every 45s rotation (SUBSET_ROTATE_MS). Confirmed via repeated live testing: a bare 'requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(resolve))' check hangs 30+ seconds on a FRESH /memorial page load with zero scrolling -- meaning the main thread is blocked by synchronous JS, not just heavy paint/animation. This matches independent 'frozen compositor/rAF' complaints from at least 2 other agents this session on this same page. Likely made worse by the newly-added avoidBoxes exclusion region for the message legibility fix (harder to place names -> more failed attempts before giving up -> worse worst-case cost).

Fix needed before shipping: reduce algorithmic cost (spatial index/grid instead of O(n) linear scan per attempt against all placed+avoid boxes; lower maxAttempts with a sane fallback instead of exhausting 280 attempts per name; and/or chunk placement across multiple animation frames via requestIdleCallback/rAF batching instead of one giant synchronous pass) so initial mount and each 45s rotation complete fast enough to never block the main thread noticeably (target: sub-frame-budget increments, no single synchronous block over ~50ms). Verify by confirming rAF scheduling stays responsive (no multi-second hangs) on a fresh load AND across at least one rotation cycle.
close_reason: Memorial wall perf fix verified: spatial-grid packing + canvas-based text measurement (was DOM getBoundingClientRect forced-layout per name), confirmed sub-20ms pack time live with real 1672-name dataset, no long tasks over a 45s rotation cycle, typecheck+tests clean.

title: [bug] Home hero map clips on scroll — fixed plate clamps to viewport top leaving a clipped band
description: On '/', the persistent .ds-map-stage plate is position:fixed and inset to the hero panel via applyHeroMapInset/heroMapStageGeometryForRect (apps/web/src/lib/map-experience/hero-map-inset.ts). On scroll, heroMapStageGeometryForRect clamps visibleTop=Math.max(0,rect.top), so as the hero panel scrolls up (panel.top goes negative), the stage top pins to 0 and height shrinks (verified: at scrollY=500, stage top:0 h:125 while panel.top:-341 panelBottom:125). Result: the map does not scroll away with the hero; it leaves a shrinking clipped strip pinned at the top of the viewport that peeks around/under the sticky nav — reads as 'the map clips on scroll'. Fix: let the plate scroll away cleanly with the hero panel (or fade/hide before it becomes a clipped sliver) instead of clamping to top:0. Verify on / at desktop width by scrolling past the hero and confirming no clipped map band remains under the nav. Repro found live 2026-07-24.
close_reason: Fixed hero map clip-on-scroll: heroMapStageGeometryForRect now tracks the full hero panel box (top may be negative) so the fixed MapStage plate scrolls away with the hero instead of clamping top to 0 and shrinking into a clipped band; hide-ratio now computed against true viewport overlap so it trips correctly. Verified live at 1440w light+dark: scrollY 0 stage overlays panel (159/466, no regression), 300 tracks panel (-141/466), 500 tracks (-341/466) vs old (0/125) clipped band, 600 hidden. Web typecheck + 983 tests pass.

title: Entity completeness audit + backfill/discovery run
description: Post-cleanup execution run with three parts. (1) AUDIT FIRST: enumerate every field the entity page actually renders (apps/web/src/app/entity/[id]/ and mobile equivalent) and the claim classes the domain expects (summary, historicalContext, era buckets, location + precision, topics, images/media, related entities, sources), then measure null/blank rates across all 1,383 bb_canonical entities and the active release projection — output a per-field, per-kind completeness report (the owner sees several blank elements on entity pages today; quantify exactly which fields are empty and for how many entities). (2) BACKFILL: run the existing enrichment lanes (gap-fill research, editorial-enrichment) prioritized BY the audit — worst load-bearing fields first (whatever renders blank on the page beats invisible metadata), staged for review, never auto-published. (3) DISCOVER: run entity discovery for new candidates — the curated cultural-figures lane from repo-xez5.6 (Lorde, Baldwin, hooks, Hansberry, plus roster) and, once repo-xez5.3/.4 land, authority-graph expansion from existing entities. Outcome must INCLUDE the audit report (docs/research/ or a bead comment): before/after completeness numbers, entities touched, candidates staged, and a ranked list of remaining blanks with why (no source found vs lane missing vs rights-gated).
acceptance_criteria: A written completeness report exists with per-field/per-kind blank rates before and after; backfill drafts staged for review with provenance for the worst fields; new-entity candidates staged including the named missing figures; nothing published without review; report ends with a prioritized remaining-gaps list.
notes: Execution model: Haiku fan-out for the field-completeness audit queries and per-entity backfill batches (mechanical, review-gated); Sonnet writes the audit report, sets backfill priorities, and reviews staged output quality. LLM-lane note: within the research harness itself, use the free/local tier per repo-xez5.2 for extraction and the strong paid tier only for prose drafts.
close_reason: Audit report written (docs/research/entity-completeness-audit.md): primary_image 95% blank, taxonomy 100% blank non-place, related 74% blank (root cause: sparse entity_relationships), historicalContext 37% blank on DC place import. Backfill sample (10 entities, mock provider, unstaged) and discovery for 4 named figures (staged via research-intake, pending_review) done. Committed 72c46dbb.

title: Single source of truth: eliminate entity duplication across fixtures, Firestore, Supabase, and code
description: Entities currently exist in four places with unclear precedence: (1) git fixtures — packages/firebase/fixtures/national-catalog/ (118 files: starter seeds + auto-promoted campaign chunks), effectively a source-of-truth-in-code; (2) Firestore canonicalEntities — still the publish path (publish-national-catalog.ts per repo-qc8w notes) despite ADR-020 (accepted 2026-07-20, reconciled 2026-07-22) declaring Firestore 'export/rollback/utilities only'; (3) Supabase bb_canonical.entities — the declared system of record (1,383 rows live); (4) hand-curated entity data in CODE — MENTION_OVERRIDES map in packages/domain/src/graph/mention-resolver.ts:55, the SearXNG query roster packages/config/src/scheduled-jobs/data/corsair-web-search-queries.json, and any similar in-source rosters. Work: (a) write the precedence rule down once (extend ADR-020 or a short ADR): Supabase bb_canonical is SoR; fixtures are one-way SEED INPUT consumed by an import lane, never re-exported, never hand-edited after import (or: archived after promotion); Firestore path retired per the ADR-020 wind-down checklist; (b) audit and reconcile drift between the 118 fixture files, Firestore, and bb_canonical (row counts, ids, claim divergence) with a report; (c) migrate in-code entity tables (MENTION_OVERRIDES, query rosters) into data (bb_ops or bb_reference) with provenance, loaded at runtime, so curation edits do not require code deploys; (d) verify apparent projection duplication is by-design: bb_public.release_entities=2742 and release_stories showing each story twice are consistent with immutable per-release projections (ADR-004) ONLY if exactly N releases exist — confirm against bb_publication.releases and active_release, document, and add a uniqueness check (release_id, entity/slug) so real dupes cannot hide; (e) delete or quarantine superseded fixture chunks once the import lane is authoritative. Related: repo-atya (ledger cutover), repo-2ztn (closed data-landscape epic), repo-bhfd (public releases from canonical ledger).
acceptance_criteria: A written precedence rule exists and CI-checkable: no path writes entities to two stores; fixtures import one-way with an audit report of reconciled drift; MENTION_OVERRIDES and query rosters live in data with provenance and code reads them at runtime; per-release projection uniqueness constraint or check exists; Firestore entity-write paths are removed or gated behind the documented rollback flag.
notes: Execution model: Sonnet only for precedence rule + migration paths (destructive-adjacent). Haiku fan-out acceptable for the read-only drift audit (comparing fixture chunks vs Firestore vs bb_canonical in batches).
close_reason: Precedence rule written, drift audit done, MENTION_OVERRIDES moved to data, release dup verified as N=2 releases + uniqueness constraints applied. Committed b01bee6b.

description: There is currently no mechanism that takes an entity and finds its network — discovery is fixture-first and mention-based (packages/domain/src/graph/mention-resolver.ts). description: Today routing is ad-hoc env config (EDITORIAL_LLM_PROVIDER, OPENROUTER_MODELS, STORY_REWRITE_MODEL(S)) with no per-task policy, and bb_research.model_invocations has 0 rows. title: Research methodology v2: portable harness, entity network expansion, multi-decade evidence spine
description: Umbrella for upgrading the research pattern based on a full audit (2026-07-24) of the pipeline, live Supabase ledger, and external scholarship (Colored Conventions principles, Gallon's Black DH 'technology of recovery', Enslaved.org PROV/uncertainty practices, Mapping Inequality/NCRC/Aaronson et al. redlining methodology). Findings driving this epic: (1) Corsair's personal Tailscale IP is baked into .env.example, worker-preflight fallback, and overnight/discovery scripts, making one operator's machine an implicit default; (2) bb_canonical.entity_identifiers has 0 rows — no Wikidata/LCNAF/SNAC anchors, so there is no machine path to expand from an entity to its network (Audre Lorde, James Baldwin, bell hooks, Lorraine Hansberry all absent from 1,383 canonical entities); (3) relationships are sparse (543 edges; authored=2, depicts=1) vs a 20-type taxonomy; (4) statistical series are mostly 2018-2024 snapshots — multi-decade spines exist only for Vera jails 1970-2024, SCF wealth 1989-2022, census 1790-1990 national/state (county historical table empty), blocking decade-scale storytelling beyond the Chicago redlining pilot; (5) model routing has no task->tier policy in code and bb_research.model_invocations is never written, so cost/quality tradeoffs are invisible; (6) gap analysis measures only state x decade vs DPLA, not entity completeness, figure-category coverage, or theme evidence sufficiency.
acceptance_criteria: A contributor without Corsair can run the full research harness with documented defaults; entity expansion from external authorities produces staged (never auto-published) candidates and demonstrably surfaces the Audre Lorde network; every LLM call is logged with model+cost tier; theme storytelling has a documented multi-decade data checklist and at least one non-Chicago theme meets it; methodology docs codify naming/dignity, uncertainty, and community-review principles from cited scholarship.

close_reason: All 12 children complete: docs purge + carryover, Corsair de-hardcoded, model routing + cost logging, Wikidata/LCNAF/SNAC anchors (628 reconciled), network expansion engine (Audre Lorde pilot), claims-mining edges, figures lane + gap metrics, Detroit evidence spine + publishability checklist, scholarship principles doc, agent-agnostic harness docs, entity SoT precedence, completeness audit + backfill + discovery for 4 named figures.

title: Cinematic Map Backdrop — adopt Pattern D sitewide (web + mobile)
description:
Generalize the chosen hero pattern ('Option D') into ONE reusable, cross-surface interaction model: a persistent map plate behind page content that is LOCKED until the reader taps 'Explore the map', with an optional short scroll-driven camera intro on landing/narrative surfaces, and a single-feature selection that pulses one ring and never flashes neighbors.

Canonical spec (READ FIRST, every child cites a section): docs/ui/patterns-cinematic-map.md. Design governance: docs/ui/README.md pattern index, docs/ui/patterns-registry.md, docs/ui/brand.md (flat matte, copper discipline), docs/ui/story.md (voice). Builds on patterns-map-canvas.md (persistent MapStage, ADR-017) and patterns-map-entity-encoding.md.

Three states (identical web + mobile): Rest (locked, dimmed, framed) -> Invite (scroll flies the camera between beats, still locked; landing/narrative only) -> Engaged (tap to unlock hands-on; Close/Escape relocks, deselects, restores home camera). See spec §1-2.

Motion reuses existing camera grammar (web camera-presets.ts, mobile mapCamera.ts) and --ds tokens; reduced motion turns flights into cuts (spec §3). A11y: keyboard, focus move on engage/close, 44px targets, no color-alone (spec §4).

Reference implementations land FIRST on '/' (web) and the mobile Explore tab; other surfaces adopt after. Depends on the two paint-stability bug fixes (repo-96j2 mobile flash, repo-mrmh neighbor flash) — those are the selection guarantee this pattern needs.

Definition of done: reusable cinematic-map module exists (web) with tests; home + mobile Explore adopt it; selection is single-feature on both platforms; reduced-motion + a11y verified; docs cross-referenced. Sized into small, self-contained child beads below.

title: Deselecting an entity makes neighbouring markers flash / reset state
description:
When a user exits/deselects an entity, nearby entities appear to flash or reset state. Root cause: selection teardown re-runs paint for every marker instead of just the affected one. reconcileSelection (apps/mobile/src/features/explore/selection.ts) plus the availableReconciled and the deselect effect in ExploreView.tsx (~lines 197-202) fire entityDeselected on incidental filter/source churn; combined with the full-source selection filter re-encode (see repo-96j2), the whole entity layer repaints, so neighbours blink.

Fix direction: scope selection/deselection to a single-feature update (feature-state or a separate selection source layer) so exiting an entity mutates only that feature's paint; guard reconciliation so it does not dispatch entityDeselected unless the selected entity is genuinely withdrawn; ensure camera commands (token-guarded already in MapScreen ~191-224) are not the trigger. Web equivalent: apps/web selection layers should also toggle a single feature, not re-filter the source.

Acceptance: selecting then deselecting an entity leaves every other marker visually untouched (no opacity/scale blink). Verify mobile via 'pnpm mobile:ios:verify'.

Files: apps/mobile/src/features/explore/selection.ts, apps/mobile/src/features/explore/ExploreView.tsx, apps/mobile/src/features/explore/explore-controller.ts, apps/mobile/src/features/map/MapScreen.tsx
close_reason: Same root-cause fix as repo-96j2: selection/deselection now only updates the filter on two always-mounted Layers instead of mounting/unmounting them, so neighboring markers are never repainted. reconcileSelection/selection.ts and the ExploreView deselect effect already guarded correctly (content-based .some checks, no spurious dispatch) — confirmed by reading selection.ts and explore-controller.ts. Verified via unit tests, typecheck, lint, and a real Release build; manually selected/deselected an entity on Simulator without error.

title: Mobile hero map flashes as if reloading on initial paint / selection change
description:
On mobile the hero/Explore map visibly flashes as if it is trying to load. Root cause: the MapLibre GeoJSONSource is re-encoded on first paint and again whenever selectedEntityId changes. The selection layers (ENTITY_SELECTED_LAYER_STYLE / ENTITY_SELECTED_INNER_LAYER_STYLE in apps/mobile/src/features/map/entity-paint.ts) use filter expressions like ['==', ['get','entityId'], selectedEntityId], which forces MapLibre to repaint against the whole source rather than toggling a single feature's paint. Combined with a possible non-memoized filteredMapSource / enrichMapFeatureCollection call in apps/mobile/src/features/map/MapScreen.tsx (~line 187, 356), the source re-encodes on mount and on selection.

Fix direction: keep the map mounted and the source stable; drive selection via a feature-state or a dedicated single-feature selection source instead of a full-source filter re-encode; memoize the enriched feature collection so identity is stable across renders. Verify on a real Release build via 'pnpm mobile:ios:verify' (not Metro).

Files: apps/mobile/src/features/map/MapScreen.tsx, apps/mobile/src/features/map/entity-paint.ts, apps/mobile/src/features/explore/ExploreView.tsx
close_reason: Fixed: entity-selected/-inner Layers in MapScreen.tsx are now always mounted (never conditionally added/removed based on selectedEntityId), and the selection filter is memoized on selectedEntityId alone. This stops the GeoJSONSource children shape from changing on mount/selection, which was forcing a full-source re-encode/repaint. Verified via unit tests (1003 passing), typecheck, lint, and a real Release build running on iOS Simulator.

title: Dev client cannot reach Supabase: api.blackbook.app NXDOMAIN + Explore uses DEMO_MAP_SOURCE
description:
## Symptom
BlackStory (Dev) iOS client appears not to hit Supabase / live entities.

## Root cause (verified 2026-07-22 on feat/mobile-launch)
1. **Explore map/list never calls the network.** `ExploreView` / `explore.tsx` default `source` to `DEMO_MAP_SOURCE` (hardcoded fixture GeoJSON in `src/features/map/demoMapSource.ts`). ADR-025 target is redacted GeoJSON from api-public, but there is **no** `/v1/map` (or similar) route in `apps/api-public` today — only health/compatibility/bootstrap/entity/search.
2. **Learn** uses bundled `content-catalog.ts`, not API.
3. **Search / entity / bootstrap** DO call `extra.apiBaseUrl` (default `https://api.blackbook.app`) via `createDefaultApiClient` → transport. But:
   - `api.blackbook.app` is **NXDOMAIN** (no DNS A/CNAME at 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1).
   - Cloud Run project `black-book-efaaf` has **no** `black-book-api-public` service deployed (only admin + discovery jobs).
4. **AppProviders** swallows runtime/bootstrap failures (`catch { setRuntime(null) }`) with no Metro log — looks like "empty app" / fixtures forever.
5. Web Explore reads Postgres **server-side** (`PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=postgres` + `DATABASE_URL` in Next.js), not via `api.blackbook.app`. Mobile cannot use that path (ADR-022).

## Fix tracks
- Infra: provision DNS + deploy `apps/api-public` to Cloud Run behind Armor (`infra/gcp/armor`).
- Product: wire Explore to a release-coupled map GeoJSON endpoint once it exists; until then document DEMO fixtures.
- Dev UX: log API base URL + bootstrap sync result in `__DEV__` (do not leave silent).

## Local verify (until prod host exists)
```bash
# Terminal A — api-public against Supabase
cd apps/api-public
run-with-dev-secrets -- env PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=postgres DATABASE_SSL=1 pnpm dev
# listens :8080

curl -sS -H 'X-BlackStory-Client: mobile/1.0.0; api=1' http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/bootstrap | jq .
curl -sS -H 'X-BlackStory-Client: mobile/1.0.0; api=1' 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/search?q=black&pageSize=5' | jq .

# Terminal B — mobile Dev pointed at LAN IP (not localhost on device)
# apps/mobile/.env.local:
# API_BASE_URL=http://192.168.x.x:8080
cd apps/mobile && npx expo start --dev-client --clear
```
Metro should log `[blackstory] apiBaseUrl=…` and `[blackstory] bootstrapSync=…`.
notes: Product track done in-repo (repo-hr62 + repo-95ct). Remaining: DNS/Cloud Run (repo-crcg) + human SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY (repo-hxjj). Local verify still needs API_BASE_URL → LAN api-public.

title: MOB-017 follow-up: device VoiceOver/TalkBack manual test pass for the automated a11y wiring
description:
Outcome
A human tester confirms on real iOS (VoiceOver) and Android (TalkBack) hardware that the
announce/focus/touch-target/selected-state wiring landed for MOB-017 actually produces the
intended assistive-tech behavior — automated RNTL assertions in this session prove the React
props are set correctly, but cannot prove VoiceOver/TalkBack's actual on-device announcement
timing, rotor/traversal order, or double-tap target size "feel".

Scope (what this session's automated pass covers, that still needs a device pass)
1. Notice/ErrorState: useAnnounceOnMount now fires announceForAccessibility on mount everywhere
   accessibilityLiveRegion is used (that prop is Android-only per RN's own docs) — confirm
   VoiceOver actually announces a freshly-mounted Notice/ErrorState on a real iPhone, and that
   TalkBack's live-region announcement and this hook's announcement don't double-announce in an
   annoying way in practice.
2. EntityPreviewSheet / CorrectionReceipt: useAccessibilityFocus calls
   AccessibilityInfo.sendAccessibilityEvent(handle, 'focus') when the sheet/receipt mounts in
   place. Confirm VoiceOver/TalkBack focus actually visibly lands on the panel (not just that the
   API was called) when tapping a map pin/list row, and when a correction is submitted.
3. CorrectionForm ChipRow/Checkbox: now have minHeight 44 and accessibilityRole/State. Confirm
   real double-tap hit target feels right at Dynamic Type / large-text sizes, and that
   VoiceOver/TalkBack announce "selected"/"checked" correctly when swiping through them.
4. filters-sheet kind picker: now exposes accessibilityRole="radio" +
   accessibilityState.selected instead of a "✓ " label prefix. Confirm VoiceOver's rotor and
   TalkBack's traversal announce selection correctly and that no regression was introduced versus
   the old label-based affordance for sighted users.

Non-goals
This bead is scoped to the device-verification pass for the specific wiring above. It is NOT the
full MOB-017 audit (Dynamic Type matrix, reduced motion, contrast, tablet/orientation, Switch
Access/Voice Control, Accessibility Inspector/Scanner reports) — those remain open under
MOB-017 itself and are not claimed as covered by this bead.

Tests
Manual VoiceOver script (iOS) and TalkBack script (Android) covering the 4 scope items above, one
recording/screenshot set per platform per item, attached as evidence to close.

Evidence to close
Device recordings or screenshots for both platforms covering all 4 items, plus written
confirmation of pass/fail per item.

title: Fix pre-existing typecheck errors in mobile entity test files (blocks Mobile Typecheck CI gate)
description:
Outcome
The new CI job \"Mobile Typecheck\" (black-book-mobile-019, .github/workflows/ci.yml) is real
and correctly failing against these pre-existing bugs discovered while wiring it up — it is
not something the CI-wiring bead is scoped to fix (apps/mobile/src is out of MOB-019's
exclusive path ownership).

Scope
apps/mobile/src/features/entity/__tests__/EntityDetailScreen.accessibility.test.tsx and
apps/mobile/src/features/entity/__tests__/useEntityDetail.test.ts only.

Findings (reproduced with `npm run typecheck` in apps/mobile after a clean `npm ci` +
regenerating the gitignored expo-env.d.ts shim; jest itself is fully green — 629/629 — because
jest transpiles via Babel and never type-checks, so this is TS-only, not a runtime bug):

1. EntityDetailScreen.accessibility.test.tsx: `headingLevelsInOrder(root: ReturnType<typeof
   render>)` types `root` as the *Promise* `@testing-library/react-native`'s `render` returns,
   but every call site does `const root = await render(...)` and passes the *resolved* value.
   4 errors (TS2339 / TS2345 x3) at lines 41, 54, 61, 71. Fix: type the parameter as
   `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof render>>` (or a local type alias), not `ReturnType<typeof render>`.
2. useEntityDetail.test.ts: three `await rerender()` calls (lines 40-42, i.e. the 3rd test's
   `rerender()`/two more in the same block) pass zero arguments, but this
   `@testing-library/react-native` version's `rerender` signature requires the new
   element/component argument (TS2554 x3). Fix: pass the same hook-invoking element/callback
   used in the initial `renderHook(...)` call (check current `@testing-library/react-native`
   docs for the exact `rerender` signature at the installed version — do not guess a
   placeholder argument).

Tests
`cd apps/mobile && npm run typecheck` must exit 0 with zero errors. `npm test -- --ci` must
stay at 629/629 (already green — do not regress it while fixing types).

Evidence to close
Clean `npm run typecheck` + `npm test -- --ci` output pasted into the closing comment.
notes: Filed while executing black-book-mobile-019 (mobile CI quality gates). Once closed, black-book-mobile-019's Mobile Typecheck job can be proposed as a required branch-protection status check (infra/github/rulesets/main-protection.json — a separate integrator's exclusive path, not touched by MOB-019).
close_reason: Fixed: regenerated the gitignored expo-env.d.ts shim (tsconfig.json's tsc run was failing before ever reaching tsconfig.tooling.json, which is what actually type-checks test files, due to two unrelated missing-module errors from the missing shim) then fixed the two reported bugs verbatim: EntityDetailScreen.accessibility.test.tsx's headingLevelsInOrder(root) now types root as Awaited<ReturnType<typeof render>> instead of the un-awaited Promise type; useEntityDetail.test.ts's three bare rerender() calls now pass rerender(undefined) to satisfy this @testing-library/react-native@14.0.1 version's typed (props: Props) => Promise<void> rerender signature. Evidence: npm run typecheck exits 0 with zero errors; npm test -- --ci is 646/646 (629 baseline + 17 new MOB-017 tests), no regressions.

title: Security decision: limited-use App Check tokens for MOB-016 correction-submission replay resistance
description: MOB-016's correction-submission client uses a STANDARD (multi-use) App Check token, not a limited-use/single-consumption token. Replay resistance today rests only on rate-limiting plus a deterministic content-hash idempotency key, not a true single-use token. Owner/security decision needed: is a limited-use token mandatory before shipping the corrections write path, or is rate-limit + content-hash dedup an accepted sufficient control?
notes:
Security decision (2026-07-20): ACCEPT standard App Check token + layered controls for staging/MOB-016 e2e; defer client limited-use token to pre-production hardening.

Rationale:
1. Server already enforces replayProtection:true (Admin SDK consume-once) in apps/api-submissions/src/app-check.ts — replays surface as replayed_token / 401 app_check_required.

This conflicts with the free-tier-first posture (ADR-023 §7). Decision needed: either (a) accept un-signed OTA on the free tier with compensating controls (MFA custody + scoped CI-only EAS token + staged rollout + immutable-update rollback) and record it as an accepted risk, or (b) budget for a paid EAS plan to enable code signing. notes:
DECISION (already made in ADR-023's 2026-07-20 adversarial-review amendment; this bead implements it): free-tier accepted-risk. EAS Update code signing is a paid EAS Production/Enterprise-plan feature, not an SDK-support gap. To keep the free-tier-first posture (ADR-023 S7), OTA ships WITHOUT end-to-end code signing on the free tier. Blast-radius controls (threat-model T6): phishing-resistant MFA custody of the EAS org, a scoped/revocable CI-only publish token, staged channel rollout, immutable-update rollback (republish previous update, never a hotfix in place). Activates with zero code change once EAS_PROJECT_ID is set.
- eas.json: verified already correct -- development/preview/production build profiles each declare a distinct `channel`, satisfying ADR-023 S1's environment-boundary requirement. No change needed.
- New apps/mobile/src/updates/ module (config.ts, native-bridge.ts, bootstrap.ts, index.ts + tests, 11 tests passing): pure posture resolver + defensive guarded-require native loader (mirrors src/security/app-check.ts / src/observability/native-bridge.ts pattern) + checkForUpdate/fetchAndApplyUpdate wrappers that never throw. - apps/mobile/src/updates/README.md: full decision record, human-gate activation steps (eas init -> set EAS_PROJECT_ID -> eas update:configure -> MFA custody), MFA custody requirements, CI-scoped-token requirements, and the OTA rollback runbook (ADR-023 S6, to be drilled by MOB-021).

title: Epic: Entity interconnectedness — relationship backfill + wire-forward
description:
## Problem
Related entities in the national catalog are not linked. Measured across packages/firebase/fixtures/national-catalog/: 771 entities, only 46 (~6%) have any related[] edges; ~725 are isolated. March on Washington is not tied to MLK; MLK is not tied to the Civil Rights Movement/SCLC/SNCC or the laws/cases those struggles produced. Goal: surface the interconnectedness of Black history through time so that even without state outlines the dots and lines trace the shape of the U.S.

## Root cause: data, not code
The relationship infrastructure already exists and works — typed edge model (entityRelationships, 20 types, evidence-required), extraction (extractCatalogRelationships in packages/domain/src/graph/catalog-related.ts), projection/adjacency, publish pipeline (packages/firebase/scripts/publish-national-catalog.ts), graph+map UI, and Gemini vector stack (entityEmbeddings, findNearest). The catalog fixtures simply contain almost no related[] edges, and mentionedEntityIds (on 49 entities) is not read by extraction.

## Target
Backfill evidence-backed edges for the 771 existing entities and wire the pipeline so new entities arrive connected. Acceptance: one dominant connected component covering >=95% of publishable entities, zero isolated publishable entities, median degree >= target.

## Decisions (owner)
1) New standalone epic, dependency-linked to repo-tt2u/repo-008877ad/repo-4ec6.
2) Provision Gemini key + embeddings backfill FIRST, then vector KNN is the primary candidate generator.
3) Full sweep of all 771 entities.
4) Tiered validation gate: deterministic edges auto-accept; LLM-proposed edges adversarially cross-checked; high-impact/living-person edges human-reviewed. LLMs never self-approve/publish.

## Principles
No assumptions; every published edge evidence-backed and (if LLM-proposed) adversarially refuted. Git-durable authoring: edges written as related[] into fixtures, Firestore populated by re-running publish. Cheap subagents fan out; Opus coordinates.

title: Fix unstable_cache 2MB overflow for live public entities
description:
## Outcome
Stop Next.js console failures when live entity catalogs exceed the 2MB data-cache limit while preserving correct map/search/history behavior and public-data dignity boundaries.

## Context
`listPublicEntityViews` → `loadLiveEntities` → `cachedLiveEntities` puts the full hydrated entity array in `unstable_cache`. Payloads ~2.4MB fail with: items over 2MB can not be cached.

## Acceptance
- Oversized live entity payloads no longer attempt to store the full array in Next data cache
- Map/search/history consumers still get correct public entity views
- No private data leaked into public cache
- Focused unit tests for public-data / map loading pass
acceptance_criteria: Oversized live catalogs do not blow Next 2MB cache; public consumers still correct; tests pass
close_reason: Fixed Next.js 2MB unstable_cache overflow for live public entity catalogs. Size-gate stores only a tiny oversized sentinel in Next data cache; fat payloads live in process-local TTL memory (public projections only). Added live-catalog-cache helpers + unit tests; public-data/map tests pass (30/30).

title: Align /history graph with site encoding + adaptive density
description:
## Outcome
Fix the /history relationship viz so it follows site design patterns and stays readable at catalog scale.

## Problems
1. Force-plot of up to 80 labeled nodes becomes a hairball with real data volume.
2. Nodes use ink fill instead of shared kind shade+glyph encoding from kind-encoding.ts / map legend.
3. Overview kind bars also use flat ink, inconsistent with KindBadge/map colors.

## Approach
1. Adaptive modes: aggregate kind hubs (default when many records), ego-neighborhood when a record is selected, full record graph only when filtered set is small (≤~24).
2. Always paint with kindEncodingFor shade + glyph; selection = copper ring; never invent new palette.
3. Labels only when sparse or on selected node; aggregate mode labels kinds + counts.
4. Compact kind legend reusing ds-legend-glyph vocabulary.

title: Resolve App Check outage fail-open/closed conflict: threat model vs @repo/security rate-limits
description: Mobile threat model (docs/mobile/security/threat-model.md, Threat 2) requires read endpoints to fail OPEN (degrade to rate-limited anonymous access) during an App Check outage or transient attestation failure, so a legitimate-but-unattested client isn't locked out. But the EXISTING shared packages/security/src/rate-limits.ts (lines ~476-482, evaluateQuota) hard-denies any 'expensive_read' cost-tier request (e.g. search) with app_check_required for callers without a verified App Check token - there is no outage/degraded-mode carve-out today. This is not mobile-specific: apps/api-public's real search endpoint (built in MOB-004) inherits this exact behavior today, and it's shared code apps/web could also depend on. Fixing it means changing platform-wide security policy (packages/security), which is a judgment call for the security/owner review, not something to change unilaterally inside the mobile program. Options: (a) add an explicit outage-detection signal that relaxes expensive_read to rate-limited-anonymous only when App Check's own service is confirmed down (not just an unverified token), (b) accept current hard-deny behavior for expensive_read and revise the threat model's fail-open claim to apply only to static_read (which is already correctly ungated today), (c) something else. Needs an explicit decision, then a small, reviewed change to packages/security if (a) is chosen.
notes:
RESOLVED (2026-07-20). Decision: option (a) — explicit outage signal + bounded degraded search. Attestation != authorization; fail-open for availability must not become free enumeration.

Policy implemented in @repo/security (rate-limits.ts evaluateQuota):
- NORMAL operation unchanged: unattested anonymous expensive_read/mutation still hard-denied app_check_required (enumeration/abuse defense). This is correct and must stay — relaxing it unconditionally would make /v1/search free enumeration for any tokenless caller.
- New explicit input RateLimitEvaluateInput.appCheckAvailability: 'available' (default) | 'outage'. Only a systemic operator/circuit signal sets 'outage' — never a single unverified request.
- Under 'outage', the expensive_read/mutation hard-deny relaxes to a BOUNDED DEGRADED quota via deriveOutageDegradedPolicy (~1/4 of anonymous caps, floored at 1, single concurrency) instead of a hard deny — matches ADR-020 §3 / threat-model T2 fail-open intent without free access.
- risk_score_exceeded still fails CLOSED during an outage (abuse SIGNAL crossing threshold, not mere token absence). Static reads never hit the deny → fail open in all modes. Attested callers keep full quota even during outage. Allowed decisions carry degraded:true for observability/T2 evidence.

Wiring: apps/api-public rate-limits.ts threads appCheckAvailability into the evaluator; handlers.ts adds optional HandlerDeps.appCheckAvailability provider (defaults 'available' → zero behavior change today). Wire it to an operator kill-switch flag or App Check verification circuit breaker.

Scope note / follow-up: distinguishing a genuine App Check OUTAGE from an individually-unverified caller requires an operator/circuit input today because @repo/firebase's createAppCheckGuard maps a verifier throw to 'invalid_token' (no 'outage' reason surfaced). Auto-detection (circuit breaker on verifier failures emitting an outage signal) is a follow-up in @repo/firebase scope — out of this bead's exclusive paths.

Files changed (exclusive scope only): packages/security/src/{rate-limits.ts,rate-limits.test.ts,index.ts}; apps/api-public/src/{rate-limits.ts,http/handlers.ts,http/handlers.test.ts,http/README.md}.

Validation: @repo/security 88 tests pass (7 new outage tests) + tsc typecheck clean; apps/api-public 59 tests pass (2 new repo-uqmm handler tests) + tsc typecheck clean. (Worktree had a corrupted @types+node@22.20.1 store entry breaking all package typechecks; repaired locally to run the real gates, then restored exactly.)

Docs: left docs/adr + threat-model unedited per task instruction (prefer bead notes + code comments). ADR-020 §3 and threat-model T2 currently cite this bead as OPEN with fail-open scoped to static reads; owner/mobile-program should update those to reflect that expensive_read now fails open (bounded degraded) on a confirmed outage. Resolution is documented at file tops (rate-limits.ts, handlers.ts) and in apps/api-public/src/http/README.md. No commit/push per instructions.

title: Honest why-this-appears: cite sources, not internal rubric alone
description:
## Problem statement
Public entity pages render a "Why this appears" / notability basis block on nearly every record. For seed and many projected records the basis is synthesized from `notabilityLabels` with empty `evidenceIds`, while adapters inject generic thematic/geographic "evidence" that is not a source citation. Readers see an auditable-sounding inclusion claim without checkable references. That is inaccurate relative to how the corpus was assembled (resourced/ingested from external sources) and reads as dishonest or unneeded boilerplate.

## Why necessary
Brand and product invariants require evidence before assertion, citations on public claims, and no completeness/authority overclaim. Inclusion reasons must resolve to retained source evidence, not BlackStory-internal rubric text alone.

## Verified current behavior
- `apps/web/src/app/entity/[id]/page.tsx` always mounts Relevance / Why this appears when `buildWhyThisAppearsForEntity` succeeds.
- `apps/web/src/app/entity/[id]/adapters.ts` synthesizes `notabilityBasis` from `notabilityLabels` with `evidenceIds: []` when structured basis is missing; injects fixed thematic + geographic RelevanceEvidence for every entity.
- `WhyThisAppears` shows criterion label + note and only a count ("N documented sources") when evidenceIds exist — not citation labels/hrefs.
- Seed entities in `public-seed.ts` have real claim citations but those are not wired into the why-appears basis UI.

## Target behavior
- Why-this-appears only asserts inclusion when linked to resolvable claim/citation evidence (source label + href when public).
- Notes explain the specific reason for this record, not a repeated rubric sentence.
- When evidence linkage is missing, show an honest gap (or omit the assertive basis), never empty-evidence "auditable" theater.
- Copy frames BlackStory as assembling/citing sources, not originating the historical facts.
- Generic topic-tag / jurisdiction metadata must not be presented as corroborating source evidence.

## Scope
Public why-appears composer, entity adapters, WhyThisAppears UI, seed/catalog projection wiring for evidenceIds→citations, tests.

## Non-goals
Full research-program rewrite; enabling new sources; changing constitution relevance gates themselves beyond honest public presentation.

## Acceptance criteria
- No public record shows "documented sources" without named, linkable citations (or explicit gap copy).
- Seed entities surface their claim citations inside why-appears basis.
- Boilerplate thematic/geographic lines are not labeled as source evidence.
- Tests cover empty evidenceIds, dangling ids, and citation rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Public why-this-appears links inclusion to real citations or honest gaps; no empty-evidence auditable theater; tests pass
notes: Implemented: release-builder claim-specific cited notes; WhyThisAppears renders named citation links; adapters rewrite rubric-only notes + wire claim evidenceIds; no topic/jurisdiction-as-evidence. Tests: domain release-builder + web WhyThisAppears + snapshot-search-index.
close_reason: Why-this-appears now shows claim-specific cited notes and named citation links; rubric-only dumps rewritten at read path; tests green. Commit 41ddbfe.

title: MOB-007: Generate native brand tokens, assets, and accessible UI primitives
description:
Outcome
The mobile app implements brand v3 through generated tokens and native primitives without copying web CSS or degrading accessibility.

Scope
Generate TypeScript color, spacing, radius, typography, motion, and logo constraints from `brand-system` source. Add native Text, Button, Link, Surface, Notice, Badge, Divider, EmptyState, ErrorState, Image, and sheet/list primitives needed by the program.

Requirements
Generated files are deterministic and never hand-edited. Preserve approved palette and flat matte rules. Bundle licensed fonts correctly and verify font licensing. Use platform-native press/focus/accessibility semantics. Support light/dark app surfaces while keeping the map's accepted fixed register unless superseded. Dynamic Type, high contrast, reduced motion, minimum touch size, loading/error/empty/offline states, and right-to-left safety are designed from the start. Logos use official assets, clear space, and minimum size.

Adversarial review
Token drift, incorrect color contrast, font fallback, missing glyphs, asset rasterization, huge font clipping, dark-mode logo inversion, accessibility label duplication, press-state invisibility, and arbitrary one-off styling. Verify no skin-tone classification or decorative anonymous portrait system enters the primitives.

Tests
Token generation snapshot; no-drift CI; unit/accessibility tests; contrast checks; font loading on both platforms; large text and dark/light screenshots; touch target assertions; screen-reader labels; asset checksum against brand source.

Model routing
Balanced design-capable coding model. Fast model may implement generator after formats are locked. Human visual approval required.

Exclusive ownership
brand token generator and apps/mobile/src/ui/**. Do not edit web UI in parallel.

Non-goals
No cross-platform component package until measured reuse warrants it.

Evidence to close

title: Visit block: map hand-off, directions, and visitable status on every record
description:
Expansion bead from the 2026-07-18 blap redesign brief (docs/ui/blap-design-direction-v4.md §5 'Visit hand-off' + §6 entity row).

Source: owner brief 2026-07-18 ('users may be using this to visit places they find here'; 'where possible should link to appropriate map tool').
Size: M
Dependencies: none (works on today's canvas; street basemap w72 improves context).

Why: the hand-off from record to real world is the product's payoff moment. A reader who found the Rosa Parks Museum must reach turn-by-turn navigation in one tap — and must never navigate to an empty lot expecting a building.

Deliver:
- Visit block on /entity/[id] (above the fold on mobile) and on explore narrative cards: 'Open in Maps' + 'Get directions' via geo: URI with Apple Maps and Google Maps web fallbacks (user-agent-appropriate ordering), built ONLY from the record's public-precision geoAnchor.
- Precision guard, fail-closed: redacted/coarse records hand off at locality/county centroid with honest labeling ('approximate area — precise site not published'); a unit test proves no sub-precision coordinate can reach a hand-off URL (extends the public-numeric/precision policy test pattern).
- Visitable status on the record: standing / rebuilt / demolished / marker-only — derived from the existing statusHistory vocabulary where present (currentEntityStatus), an explicit new status label where not; rendered as a mono-register chip in the visit block; catalog backfill for the 104-entity release (research pass reusing the 2026-07-18 provenance pattern).
- Copper discipline: the visit CTA is a primary action (copper); everything else in the block stays ink registers.

Never: exposing finer-than-public precision through ANY hand-off URL; implying a demolished site is visitable; affiliate/tracking parameters on map links.

Acceptance:
1. Rosa Parks Museum record: one tap reaches Apple/Google directions at the public coordinate, 375px both themes. 2. A locality-precision record hands off at centroid with the approximate label. 3. Precision-guard test fails the build if a redacted coordinate leaks. 4. All 104 release records carry a visitable status with a citation where the status is non-obvious. 5. a11y: links have distinguishing accessible names.

Model routing: fast model for the block + links; the status backfill research rides the established parallel-research pattern.
notes: Human bar applies (docs/ui/blap-design-direction-v4.md §2b, owner 2026-07-18): finding paths, context-carrying transitions, voice-written states, smoothness, one-tap payoff — judged alongside this bead's own acceptance list.

Size: L

Why: a visitor planning a trip starts from where THEY are ('what's near 125th and Lenox') — the archive must answer place-first questions, not only record-first ones. On mobile this becomes the primary entry into the map.

Deliver:
- One search input (explore panel + /search) with typed result groups: Records (existing search pipeline) and Places (census-geo geocode: addresses, cities, landmarks). Free-first: Census Bureau geocoder, no key; extend provider only if match quality demonstrably fails.
- Selecting a place result flies the camera via the existing presets (no new camera grammar) and shows nearby records within the flown viewport; no permanent pin is dropped.
- Debounced, cancellable requests; graceful zero-state ('No places matched — try a record search'); keyboard + screen-reader parity with the existing result list pattern.
- Geocode responses cached (same never-re-geocode-the-same-query rule as repo-40192496's cache).
- URL state: a place search that flew the camera is shareable via the existing viewport params — no new URL dimension.

Never: sending user queries to a paid geocoder by default; logging raw address queries beyond operational need (privacy posture); a second competing search UI.

Acceptance:
1. Typing '1616 Chappelle St, Tulsa' or 'Sweet Auburn Atlanta' flies to the place with nearby records visible, 375px and desktop, both themes. 2. Record search behavior unchanged and same-speed. 3. Zero-result and error states render the Notice pattern. 4. Repeat queries hit the cache (verified by request count). 5. A11y: results navigable by keyboard, announced count.

Model routing: fast model — well-specified integration against an existing adapter; escalate only if provider-quality judgment is needed.
notes:
Progress 2026-07-20:
- Root cause: Census onelineaddress only matches street addresses; City/ST returned no_match. ZIP path already worked.
- Added city/state centroid fallback (zipcodes.lookupByName → reverse geocode) in domain + web locate pipelines. Verified: Montgomery AL, Tulsa OK, New York NY, Washington DC, and street-miss → Tulsa city for 1616 Chappelle St.
- Catalog recommendations: explore place search suggests from loaded map features; /search zero-result shows “From the archive” browse picks.
- Firestore indexes added: publicSearchIndex releaseId+nameLower, releaseId+kind+nameLower, releaseId+status+nameLower (deploy via firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes).
- Remaining for full bead: /search page still record-only (no address fly-to); optional unified typeahead calling /search/api.

title: Black population by county by decade: census data model, ingestion, and map layer
description:
Owner directive 2026-07-18: pull population data at least by decade — Black population by county, decade over decade — and model the relationship between population flows (Great Migration) and entities/events. Think holistically; model data consistently across datasets.

REUSE: county join key = 5-digit FIPS already on /geo/us-counties-20m.geojson properties (stateFips+countyFips, landed 2026-07-18) and on MapCountyAggregate (packages/domain/src/map/map-source.ts); decade machinery = deriveEraBuckets (packages/domain/src/era.ts) + per-decade graph views (graph/decades.ts); presence-not-incidents dignity framing + tier philosophy = apps/web/src/lib/map-experience/density.ts (no false-absence tier) + DENSITY_TIER_FILL (dignity-style.ts); ingestion provenance = RetrievalEvent/SourceCapture (contentHash) + source registry + drift tracking (packages/domain/src/adapters/registry.ts, drift.ts); operator lane = operator-cli subcommand + thin skill (BB-085).

Data model: demographics county-decade docs {fips5, stateFips, countyFips, decade, totalPopulation, blackPopulation, source, retrievedAt, contentHash} — public census statistics (counts are fine; the non-numeric policy bans entity notability/relevance scores, not published government statistics — record that reading in the schema doc comment). One collection, keyed {fips5}_{decade}, idempotent re-ingest via contentHash.

Sources (free-first): NHGIS/IPUMS API for machine-readable historical decennial county tables 1790–2020 (needs free account + key — see companion HUMAN bead); modern slice available NOW keyless via api.census.gov decennial P.L. tables (2000/2010/2020 race by county) to prove the pipeline end-to-end before NHGIS lands.

Map/UI (follow the 6-step filter-extension recipe: url-state.ts → filters.ts applyExploreFilters → buildExploreFacetOptions → ExploreMapFeatureProperties → feature enrichment → parse/serialize): county choropleth mode on the existing density layer with a decade control tied to the era filter; joins to the county polygons already on the canvas (repo-b91695d2 county lines layer). Holistic tie-in: decade graph views + entity eraBuckets let the UI show entities/events active in the same decade as the population frame (Great Migration flows beside Bronzeville/Harlem/Greenwood records). Respect BB-051 dignity rules: population presence is the story, never deficit framing.
notes: Map layer half completed via repo-zfvj (layerMode + choropleth). Ingestion was already done. Close when operator regenerates full /geo/county-population-decades.json from Firestore.
close_reason: Verified: apps/web/public/geo/county-population-decades.json is the full operator-regenerated export (commit f5f8183d 'Wire Explore choropleths to full county population export', 2026-07-19), which was the bead's explicit close condition. Source: owner briefs 2026-07-17 (redesign) + 2026-07-18 (rebrand, full dark/light support, fully responsive, brand-pack scheme adherence).
Size: L
Dependencies: BB-097, BB-098 (in progress); gates their output plus the 2026-07-18 rename/reskin work.

Why: one gate that proves the redesign is actually done — brand-conformant, accessible, both-theme, responsive, performant — instead of per-stream self-assessment.

Deliver — four matrices, evidence committed (screenshots + traces in docs/ui/qa/):
1. BRAND-PACK CONFORMANCE: palette-only colors (5 core + 2 neutrals via tokens, no raw hex in app code); typography = Sora SemiBold headlines / Inter UI / Source Serif 4 editorial / IBM Plex Mono data (Sora landed 2026-07-18 — verify every heading register actually renders Sora); type scale within kit p.2 (H1 56/64 → caption 12/16, fluid between breakpoints); mark usage rules p.3 (clear space, min sizes 120/48/32, no separation/stretch/shadow/recolor, page-band order); copper discipline 10-15% orientation-only.
2. THEME MATRIX: every route in §6's surface inventory rendered light AND dark; AA contrast on every text/control pair in both; theme-invariant surfaces (map plate, footer, on-map header) verified deliberate; no hydration flash.
3. RESPONSIVE MATRIX: every surface at 375/768/1280; no horizontal page scroll; wide content scrolls in-container; touch targets >=44px; map surfaces one-handed usable at 375px (street zooms included once w72 lands).
4. MOTION+PERF: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation including camera flights; route-arrival + hero-dissolve within token durations; map cold load + navigation traces recorded; existing a11y test suite green.

Never: signing off from memory — every cell needs an artifact; treating dark theme or 375px as best-effort (owner: P0 findings).

Acceptance: all four matrices complete with zero open P0 findings; failures filed as beads with screenshots; gate re-runnable (scripted screenshot harness preferred over hand capture).

Model routing: fast model + scripted capture for the sweep; strong model only for judgment calls on contrast/copper findings.
design: Mirrors BB-057 for the redesign tranche. Checklists to execute: guide p.13 launch checklist (verbatim), BB-051 dignity/redaction acceptance list, contrast suite across tokens v3, reduced-motion audit of BB-098 camera work, Lighthouse mobile preset on homepage + explore, cross-browser sweep Chrome/Safari/Firefox at 375/768/1280.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every audit executed with recorded evidence (screenshots, traces, filled checklists). 2. Guide p.13 checklist passes 100%. 3. BB-051 dignity/redaction list re-verified on the new map. 4. No open P0/P1 findings from this gate. 5. A11y, contrast, and reduced-motion pass in both themes.
