title: WS5: Event-participation junction (CIDOC-CRM / Enslaved.org pattern) + kind hygiene
description:
Goal: model people/places connected THROUGH events (CIDOC-CRM E5/P11/P7/P4 junction pattern; Enslaved.org's Person/Event/Place/Source with per-event Role and Status). This is the strongest inference signal: co-participation in the same event is an auto-derivable association where the event itself is the assertion — no review needed for the derived person↔person "associated via event" connection.

### Steps

1. **Migration**: bb_canonical.event_participation (event_id → entities.id kind='event', participant_id → entities.id, role text, status_at_event text NULL, valid_edtf text NULL, evidence_ids uuid[] / claim ids, provenance). Enslaved.org rule adopted verbatim: "If Status is not known, do not record any data" — status_at_event stays NULL rather than guessed.
2. **Backfill from existing data**: convert existing occurred_at/participated_in/attended entity_relationships rows involving events into participation rows (keep the edges; participation is the richer mirror). Mine event claims for participants via mentionedEntityIds and claim subjects.
3. **Birth/death as events (optional, flagged)**: E67 Birth / E69 Death pattern — where WS3 established death with place+date (e.g. the Duluth lynchings), an event entity may already exist (lynching_* entities ARE events-as-kind in places); link victim via participation with role 'victim'. Do NOT auto-create new event entities in this pass; link to existing ones only.
4. **Inference feed**: WS4's deterministic tier gains same-event co-participation as its strongest signal; surface "connected through <event>" in the related panel (UI copy, not a new edge type).
5. **Kind hygiene found by audit**: disc_crispus_attucks_q288241 is a PERSON modeled as kind='event' with corrupted topicTags (['bobsled','abolition','bobsled',...]) — fix the kind, dedupe tags, and add a validation check for person-as-event mismatches + duplicate topicTags across the catalog.

### Acceptance

- event_participation exists, backfilled from current edges + claims; 79 events have ≥0 participants with provenance (measure coverage; target ≥50% of events with ≥1 participant).
- WS4 consumes co-participation; at least one release surface renders "through <event>" connections.
- Attucks kind fixed; catalog-wide validation reports zero person-as-event mismatches and zero duplicated topicTags.

### Guardrails

Participation rows are evidence-backed like everything else. Never infer status_at_event. No new event entities minted without review.
notes: Migration 20260729200000_event_participation applied via Supabase MCP. Backfill: 177 participation rows, 39/78 events with >=1 participant (50.0%). Attucks fixed kind person + topicTags deduped. Duluth victim links: 0 (no kind=event lynching parent exists). Co-participation helper in packages/domain/src/graph/co-participation.ts. UI viaEvent copy in EntityRelatedList. Remaining: wire co-participation into release relatedNeighbors hydration (WS4 feed).
close_reason: event_participation migrated+backfilled (39/78 events, 50%); Attucks kind fixed; kind-hygiene linter+tests; co-participation helper; EntityRelatedList through-event copy

title: entity.locationPrecision display collapses 'site' (and other precisions) to a false 'city' label
description:
apps/web/src/lib/public-data/map-projection.ts's locationPrecisionFromProjection()
only passes through 'neighborhood'|'campus'|'institution'|'county' (county added
2026-07-28); everything else -- including 'site', the precision used by the
original 47-entity and 1588-entity NRHP publish batches -- defaults to 'city'.

This means every site-precision place entity currently in production shows
"Location precision: city" on its entity page, understating how precise the
pin actually is (site is finer than city, not coarser, so this isn't a privacy
issue -- it's an honesty/UX one: the map zooms to city-scale (zoom 10) instead
of a tighter site-scale zoom, and the text claims less precision than the
data actually has).

Fix: widen PublicEntityView['locationPrecision'] (apps/web/src/data/public-seed.ts)
and its ~8 call sites (same list touched in commit b380292b) to include 'site',
give zoomForLocationPrecision('site') its own tight zoom in
apps/web/src/lib/map-experience/entity-location-map-style.ts, and update
locationPrecisionFromProjection to pass 'site' through instead of defaulting it.

Discovered while verifying the NRHP county-location reconciliation
(packages/ops-data/scripts/reconcile-nrhp-county-locations.ts, repo-jy6k).

title: Replication-verification lane + in-house corroboration computations + license audit
description:
WHY (2026-07-26 deep audit): the rigor ceiling of the chapters is set by whether we merely QUOTE academia or can VERIFY it. AEA journals mandate replication deposits (openICPSR); QJE uses Harvard Dataverse. For every causal paper we cite, the underlying data is legally downloadable — verification of the exact numbers we quote is cheap and turns 'we cite Aaronson et al.' into 'we cite them and re-checked the quoted estimates against their deposited data'. Verified anchors: AHM AEJ:Policy 2021 -> openICPSR 127803 (doi 10.3886/E127803V1), follow-up children's outcomes -> openICPSR 182585; DKKS QJE 2024 -> Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/H6NXUH + openICPSR 194203 + elloraderenoncourt.com/us-inequality-data.

SCOPE POSITION (deliberate, argued in session): verify headline numbers against packaged data = IN SCOPE (light: read their CSVs/tables, compare quoted values). Re-running full Stata/R estimation pipelines = OUT of scope unless a specific claim becomes disputed. In-house computations are corroboration and visualization only — a bug in our tract join must never be able to masquerade as a peer-reviewed finding, so derived_measurements.assumptions must state 'descriptive, not causal' and article schema should render such figures with an 'our analysis' badge.

DESIGN (Sonnet-executable):
1. Verification: per-paper mini-fixtures under packages/ops-data/fixtures/replication/<paper-slug>/ holding ONLY the extracted rows we quote (respecting package terms — cite, do not redistribute whole packages), plus a manifest with package DOI, download date, file provenance, sha256. A script packages/ops-data/scripts/verify-replication-figures.ts compares chapter/packet values to these rows; wire as optional validate step alongside repo-t6up gates.
2. HOLC computation: script joins holc_areas polygons to tract centroids (acs_tract_profiles, opportunity_atlas_tracts already keyed by tract), aggregates present-day outcomes by 1930s grade (A-D), writes derived_measurements (schema already has method_id/method_version/input_observation_ids/formula/assumptions; 45 rows exist — follow their conventions). PostGIS available in Supabase; prefer SQL over TS for the spatial join.
3. License audit: trace where holc_areas rows were ingested from (check adapter/scripts + dsl-renewing-inequality fixture lineage); Mapping Inequality georectified/spatial data = CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, scans = public domain. Deliverable is a determination + plan, not a code change.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For every ASSERT-tier causal citation in a shipped chapter, a derived_measurements row (or researchLog entry when no computation applies) records verification of each quoted headline number against the paper's replication package, with method_id, input refs, and the package DOI. 2) An in-house HOLC-grade descriptive computation exists as a reproducible script (ops-data script or adapter-style module) joining bb_reference.holc_areas x acs_tract_profiles x opportunity_atlas_tracts, outputting derived_measurements rows labeled method-stance descriptive-corroboration — and chapter copy can cite it ONLY as 'our computation over public data', never as a causal estimate. 3) A written license determination for holc_areas provenance exists (docs/data/ or bead notes): if sourced from Mapping Inequality spatial files (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), state whether product use qualifies as noncommercial; if not defensible, plan B is documented (NARA public-domain scans re-digitization or alternative dataset). 4) Verified figures: AHM openICPSR 127803 (redlining boundary effects), DKKS Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/H6NXUH / openICPSR 194203 (wealth ratios incl. 1860 56.3 and 1870 21.4), Cascio-Washington QJE 2014 and Ang AEJ:Applied 2019 for the voting chapter.

title: Casting-a-ballot chapter: causal literature is strong — assert cause with citations
description: Pre-research finding for the voting-rights chapter (repo-8602): opposite of drug policy — this has the STRONGEST causal identification of the four topics. Cascio & Washington (QJE 2014): VRA caused turnout increase and shifted state transfers. Aneja & Avenancio-León / NBER w31425: VRA narrowed Black-white wage gap (~1/5 of the 30pp Southern narrowing 1950-80 attributable). Ang (AEJ:Applied 2019) 'Do 40-Year-Old Facts Still Matter': preclearance effects persisted. Post-Shelby County (2013): peer-reviewed disparate-turnout-impact studies (J. Public Economics 2024) + documented purge/closure waves (Brennan Center, LDF). Chapter should ASSERT cause per repo-e9yj tier 1, citing these inline like buying-a-home cites Aaronson et al. Artifacts: VRA 1965 text (already have art_voting_rights_act_1965_nara binding), Shelby County v. Holder opinion, Selma-era primary docs.

title: Buying-a-home chapter: reconcile HOLC-map framing with Fishback et al. revisionist evidence
description: The chapter's spine is sound — it correctly leads with the FHA Underwriting Manual para 935 as the operative rule, and its causal cite (Aaronson/Hartley/Mazumder AEJ:Policy 2021, boundary-design neighborhood effects) survives the revisionist critique because AHM measure map-boundary effects on neighborhood trajectories, not lender behavior. But two spots imply the HOLC map guided bank lending, which Fishback/Rose/Snowden 2022 (NBER w29244; JUE 2022) directly dispute: they show HOLC refinanced Black homeowners roughly proportionately and FHA built its own redlining methodology before and independent of the HOLC maps. Fix: (1) the 1938 paragraph 'the exact same thinking has been pulled off the page and drawn onto a map... so a bank can size up a whole city in one glance' — soften to what's defensible (the maps recorded/encoded the era's appraisal doctrine; their long shadow is on neighborhoods, per AHM) or add a DisputeBlock presenting the HOLC-vs-FHA scholarly dispute honestly (component exists, currently unused here). (2) Consider whether the HOLC-map hero image caption should note FHA as the operative lender-facing mechanism. Do NOT weaken the chapter's core claim — federal redlining happened and its effects persist; the dispute is about WHICH agency's instrument did the work. This is a rigor upgrade, not a retreat.
notes: DEEP-AUDIT ADDENDUM (2026-07-26): replication anchors for the fix — AHM AEJ:Policy 2021 replication package: openICPSR project 127803, doi 10.3886/E127803V1; their children's-outcomes follow-up: openICPSR 182585. When rewriting the two HOLC-map paragraphs, the defensible formulation is: the maps ENCODED the era's appraisal doctrine and their measurable long shadow is on neighborhood trajectories (AHM boundary design); the lender-facing instrument was the FHA's own methodology (Fishback/Rose/Snowden). DisputeBlock is the preferred vehicle over silent softening.

comments.author: Gerald Dagher
comments.text: Clarification: this is NOT a case of the data not existing — BJS publishes an annual 'Prisoners in YYYY' bulletin every year back to 1926, each with a by-race imprisonment-rate table (confirmed this pattern works: pulled Table 5 from 'Prisoners in 2020' and Table 3 from 'Prisoners in 2016' this session). title: Design where entity-promotion authority lives (research case -> canonical), respecting operator-cli's proposer/approver boundary
description: The only working 'research case -> canonical entity' promotion pattern in the repo today is an untracked, gitignored ad hoc script (.cache/promote-authority-net-2026-07-23.mjs), used by hand repeatedly this session (7 real entities promoted) reusing packages/migrate-firestore-postgres's canonical-release-gate.ts logic. Attempting to formalize this as an operator-cli verb (promote-entity) during repo-348e.6 was correctly blocked: packages/operator-cli/src/promotion-boundary.test.ts proves a deliberate, tested invariant that operator-cli must never expose a promote/approve/publish/activate/retract capability — proposer and approver must be a distinct call, distinct identity, never the same package's own surface. This needs a real design decision, not a quick fix: where should promotion authority live? Options include (a) a new small package/CLI with its own auth/identity model consistent with the existing proposer/approver separation (evaluatePromotionGate pattern), reusing canonical-release-gate.ts; (b) building it into apps/admin's existing case-approval UI/API surface (which already has a real auth boundary via Supabase roles) rather than a CLI at all; (c) something else. Whichever is chosen, it should replace the untracked .cache script with committed, tested, documented tooling.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is made and documented (extend docs/decisions-carryover.md or a fresh short doc) on where promotion authority lives; a real, tested, committed implementation exists; the untracked .cache/promote-authority-net-2026-07-23.mjs pattern is no longer the only way to do this.

Group per data structure: (1) RECORD TYPE = Kind; (2) TIME & CONTEXT = Era + Status collapsed together (both temporal/contextual); (3) RELATIONSHIPS = Connections (compact toggle, it's ternary all/with/without); (4) TOPICS = Topic tags, moved into an 'Advanced/More filters' disclosure since the tag vocabulary can grow large. Target: cut perceived complexity ~40%, from 5 inline dropdowns+chips to 3-4 grouped controls. Keep Sort separate (it's ordering, not filtering). Preserve all filtering capability — this is grouping/disclosure/reduction of visual surface, not removing filter power. Verify in browser at :3048/history, light+dark, that every facet still works after regrouping.
close_reason: Filters regrouped by data structure via declarative HISTORY_FILTER_GROUPS in filters.ts: RECORD TYPE=Kind, TIME & CONTEXT=Era+Status grouped, RELATIONSHIPS=Connections compact segmented toggle, TOPICS moved into 'More filters' disclosure; Sort separated into a result bar. title: Web: selected-entity pulse ring doesn't match spec §3 (scale + reduced-motion static ring)
description:
docs/ui/patterns-cinematic-map.md §3 specifies the selection pulse as a copper ring scaling ~1→2.1 while fading opacity 0.9→0.12, with a reduced-motion fallback rendering a static enlarged ring (opacity ~0.85, scale ~1.35).

Mobile implements this correctly (apps/mobile/src/features/map/entity-paint.ts: ENTITY_SELECTED_PULSE_SCALE_FROM/TO, ENTITY_SELECTED_PULSE_OPACITY_FROM/TO, ENTITY_SELECTED_PULSE_STATIC_SCALE=1.35, ENTITY_SELECTED_PULSE_STATIC_OPACITY=0.85, wired into MapScreen.tsx's SelectedPulseRing via reduceMotion).

Web's shared MapStage (apps/web/src/app/(map)/MapStage.tsx, startSelectedEntityPulse/stopSelectedEntityPulse, ~lines 995-1039) only animates circle-stroke-opacity via rAF (0.28<->1.0 breathing) — the ring's circle-radius is a fixed static expression (markerRadiusPlusExpression(6) in apps/web/src/app/map/explore-style.ts), so there is no scale animation at all, on either normal or reduced motion. Under prefers-reduced-motion, the code just sets circle-stroke-opacity to 1 (not ~0.85) and leaves scale unchanged (not the spec's ~1.35 enlargement).

Found during QA pass repo-4v3a.10. Bring web's pulse ring (both normal motion scale/opacity curve and the reduced-motion static ring) into parity with the documented spec and the mobile reference implementation.
notes: VERIFICATION (2026-07-24, partial): Code on disk — MapStage.tsx (+58), explore-style.ts (+90), marker-size.ts modified; explore-style.test.ts updated. Web typecheck clean, 983/983 web tests pass (incl. updated pulse test). NOT confirmed: the actual animated pulse (scale 1->2.1 / opacity fade) and reduced-motion static ring are time-based visuals; the browser preview pane was unstable all session (black screenshots after scroll, inconsistent geometry reads), so I could not visually verify the ring animates or that reduced-motion renders the static 1.35/0.85 ring. NEEDS a clean visual pass: select an entity on / or /explore, watch the copper ring scale+fade loop; toggle prefers-reduced-motion and confirm static enlarged ring. Do not close until visually confirmed.

Each principle cites its source.

title: Brand tokens: surfaceRaised and inkSubtle are aliases, collapsing two design tiers
description:
apps/mobile/scripts/tokens/brand-source.ts:207 sets light surfaceRaised = surface (#FBF8F2 both), so any pressed/raised treatment built on surfaceRaised is invisible in the default light theme. Lines 210 and 234 set inkSubtle = inkMuted in BOTH themes (#6D675F light, #BDB5A9 dark), so the three-tier meta hierarchy the UI primitives assume (index inkSubtle / kicker accent / dek inkMuted) renders as two tiers everywhere.

Needs a brand decision, not a guess: light surface is already lighter than canvas, so there is no upward 'raised' step available — either surfaceRaised needs a distinct warm step, or the role should be renamed/collapsed and a real surfacePressed role added. inkSubtle needs a genuinely dimmer value that still passes the generator's contrast gates.

Worked around in repo-mkk2 by using theme.canvas as the pressed fill in ListRow/LedgerRow/Button; that is a workaround, not the fix. Edit brand-source.ts then run: pnpm --filter @repo/mobile tokens:generate (a no-drift test enforces the generated file matches).
close_reason: Light surfaceRaised (#FDFBF8), inkSubtle (#726C64/#8B857D), surfacePressed wired; tokens regenerated; no-drift + contrast tests pass.

## Goal

- App Hosting minInstances / concurrency

- Document remaining follow-ups on the bead

- High-impact public-data and App Hosting paths audited
- Safe ROI fixes implemented and tested

## Findings (audit)
- Already good: entity pages use point-get + bounded 1/2-hop neighbors (not full catalog); stories index is field-masked; story related rails use ByIds; GSP uses search index; process TTL + size-gated unstable_cache; public shell has no client Firestore (App Check only on mutate/refine routes); explore/history legitimately need full catalog (cached).

- Field-mask thin entity card projections if full docs dominate ByIds byte cost.
- Cache listPublicStoryViews if reintroduced for bulk SSG.

title: Add App Check verifier-failure circuit breaker to emit outage signal in @repo/firebase
description:
repo-uqmm (resolved, closed) added an explicit RateLimitEvaluateInput.appCheckAvailability: 'available' | 'outage' signal to @repo/security so unattested expensive_read/mutation degrades to a bounded quota during a confirmed App Check outage instead of hard-denying. Today that signal has no automatic source: @repo/firebase's createAppCheckGuard maps every verifier throw (including a genuine provider/service outage) to the same 'invalid_token' AppCheckDecision reason as an individual forged/garbage token, so apps/api-public's handlers.ts HandlerDeps.appCheckAvailability provider must be wired to a manual operator kill-switch flag, not to real verifier telemetry.

Outcome: @repo/firebase (or the api-public wiring layer) detects a sustained pattern of verifier failures consistent with a genuine App Check service outage (not a single caller's bad/missing token) and can emit 'outage' automatically, complementing (not replacing) the manual operator flag.

Scope: packages/firebase (AppCheckDecision / createAppCheckGuard) and/or apps/api-public wiring only. Do not touch packages/security's evaluateQuota policy itself (already correct per repo-uqmm).

Requirements:
- Must distinguish a systemic pattern (e.g. elevated verifier-throw rate within a rolling window, or the provider SDK's own outage signal if it exposes one) from a single unattested/invalid-token request. A lone bad token must never flip the signal to 'outage'.
- Must be a circuit-breaker style pattern (open on sustained failure rate, half-open probe, close on recovery) with a bounded, documented threshold and window, deterministic/unit-testable without live network calls.
- Must default to 'available' (current behavior) when the breaker is closed; must not change any behavior for the existing manual operator kill-switch path already wired in repo-uqmm.
- Should log/emit a metric when the breaker opens/closes for observability (MOB-018), without logging raw App Check tokens.

Tests: circuit-breaker unit tests (opens on sustained failure rate, does not open on isolated failures, closes on recovery, half-open probe behavior); apps/api-public integration test that a simulated verifier-outage pattern flips the wired appCheckAvailability provider to 'outage' and back.

Evidence to close: passing tests above, tsc clean, brief note in docs/adr/ADR-020-mobile-stack.md §3 / docs/mobile/security/threat-model.md T2 confirming automatic outage detection is live (manual doc update, not code).
notes: Filed 2026-07-20 as a docs/bd follow-up while closing out repo-uqmm's mobile-program threads (MOB-004/MOB-010 bead-hygiene pass). Not blocking MOB-004/MOB-010 close — those are gated on their own deferred-test lists (repo-rw1p, repo-shw4), not on this.
close_reason: Landed b94a990d (PR #19): @repo/firebase createAppCheckCircuitBreaker + apps/api-public resolveAppCheckAvailability wiring; APP_CHECK_OUTAGE_OVERRIDE precedence when set; 18 App Check tests (@repo/firebase app-check-circuit-breaker + app-check-enforce) + 101 api-public tests pass; ADR-020 §3 + threat-model T2 updated with automatic outage detection note.

title: MOB-022: Track measured post-launch upgrades and explicitly deferred capabilities
description:
Outcome
Deferred complexity is governed by measured triggers rather than silently entering launch scope or being forgotten.

Scope
Create child beads only when triggers are met for full offline PMTiles, push notifications, accounts/sync, saved collections, multilingual localization, tablet-specific layouts, vector search/semantic discovery, platform-specific native rewrites, or paid map services.

Requirements
Each upgrade records user outcome, measurement, trigger, cost, privacy/security expansion, migration path, rollback, and why existing architecture is insufficient. Reuse existing packages and APIs. No feature is implemented merely because a library supports it. Close or defer stale ideas explicitly.

Adversarial review
Feature creep, recurring cost, permission fatigue, account deletion burden, offline storage explosion, notification abuse, analytics-driven surveillance, and fragmented platform behavior.

Tests
Trigger evidence and design-specific tests are required in newly created beads. This bead itself verifies the post-launch metrics review cadence and backlog hygiene.

Model routing
Fast model for metric compilation; strong model only for triggered architecture/privacy decisions.

Exclusive ownership
Post-launch program tracking only.

Non-goals
This bead does not implement deferred features.

Evidence to close
30/60/90-day review entries, metrics, explicit create/defer/close decisions, synced Beads graph.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The stated outcome is demonstrably true. 2. Every requirement is implemented or explicitly rejected by an accepted ADR. 3. Adversarial cases are tested or converted into blocking follow-up beads. 4. Required automated and manual tests pass. 5. Evidence to close is attached. 6. No hidden scope expansion, server-only dependency in mobile, or unverified cloud claim remains.
notes: 2026-07-22 (owner 2C): Launch parity is epic-scoped (Explore/Search/Entity/Learn/Corrections). Explicit post-launch deferrals filed as children: repo-74oy Themes, repo-04l7 Data, repo-712h Stories. Law/History remain web-first unless measured demand adds MOB-022 children later.

The discovery adapters (RSS, Reddit, Internet Archive, DPLA, Wayback, web-search, common-crawl, census-geo, federal, wikimedia, legal) and the candidate->promotion pipeline (packages/domain/src/promotion/, packages/domain/src/extraction.ts) still emit the OLD entity shape: no entityClass/entityTypes (repo-31ec82a3), no topicIds/mentionedEntityIds/keywords/campaignIds split (repo-595ec0f2 — topicTags is deprecated but still what extraction produces), no entityNames/entityIdentifiers records (repo-fffbfe3f), no derived livingStatus signal (repo-b03d2ba4) computed at ingestion time. title: packages/domain: pnpm build fails with TS5055 dist/input collisions
description: Discovered 2026-07-18 while verifying repo-6252e3f6: 'pnpm --filter @blap/domain build' fails with dozens of TS5055 'Cannot write file dist/X.d.ts because it would overwrite input file' errors across unrelated pre-existing files (search/*, seed-campaigns/*, similarity/*, trust/*, specialized.ts). tsconfig.json itself looks correctly scoped (include: src/**/*.ts, exclude: dist), so the root cause needs deeper investigation (likely stale/orphaned dist output from files that moved, or an incremental build-info mismatch). Confirmed NOT caused by any of today's canonical-graph-alignment work: domain source-level typecheck and full test suite are both clean; this only surfaces as a symptom in apps/web's typecheck, which resolves @blap/domain via the 'types' condition (built dist/*.d.ts) rather than the 'development' condition, so a stale/broken dist causes apps/web to see outdated domain types (e.g. currently shows facts-seed.ts/legal-seed.ts missing derivedFromClaimIds even though the source already has it). dist/ is gitignored so this doesn't affect a fresh checkout's source correctness, but it does mean 'pnpm build' is currently broken for this package, which will bite real CI/publish workflows once one depends on a built dist.
notes: Root cause: src/map/generate-demo-map-source.ts (one-off script, not normal build output) imports @blap/security. Security's types depend on @blap/domain, which package.json exports resolve to dist/*.d.ts once dist exists. tsc then treats stale dist declarations as program inputs and TS5055 on re-emit. exclude dist alone does not help because dist is pulled via module resolution, not include. Fix: exclude generate-demo-map-source.ts from tsconfig build (matches file docstring). Verified: pnpm --filter @blap/domain build x2 pass; test pass.
close_reason: Excluded generate-demo-map-source.ts from tsc build; build and 1096 tests pass.

Add these plus a candidate-relationship stage (crawler/extraction creates candidates, review gates promote). Confidence rule from the validated review: graph corroboration may affect only entityMatchQuality and a separate graphConsistency diagnostic plus crawl prioritization — it must NOT raise sourceAuthority or lineageIndependence (prevents confidence-laundering a bad source through its own derived cluster; confidence engine factors verified at packages/domain/src/confidence-engine/engine.ts:27-35). Invariants: published relationship has evidence, both endpoints resolve, temporal requirements met, an edge cannot be its own sole corroboration, syndicated evidence counts once. Coordinate with repo-b9450cdf (catalog related-entry promotion) so promoted relationships carry these fields from day one.

title: BB-100: Pixel portrait system: hand-authored, code-rendered likenesses
description:
Expansion bead BB-100 from the 2026-07-17 redesign brief — exploratory, spike-gated.

Source: owner brief 2026-07-17 ("I don't think it's feasible to have a photo of everyone, but I'm curious if we could somehow do it with code, some kind of pixelated representation, and the pixels are granular enough to where you can make out who it's supposed to be. And we can do this for everyone... we can do this manually.")
Size: M (spike + system; the portrait authoring itself is ongoing human work, not part of this bead's closure)
Dependencies: BB-096

Why: photos exist for only some entities (primaryImage is optional and rights-gated; see apps/web/src/components/entity/EntityPrimaryImage.tsx). A code-rendered, hand-authored pixel-portrait system could give every person a dignified, recognizable visual identity in one consistent brand register — if and only if the spike proves recognizability and dignity hold.

Deliver:
- Design spike FIRST; everything else gates on its outcome. Establish the minimum grid granularity at which a hand-authored pixel portrait of a well-known figure is recognizable (test e.g. 16x20, 24x32, 32x40) using a brand-constrained palette (ink, charcoal, stone, sand, paper, copper accents). The palette composes portraits; it is NEVER labeled or systematized as a skin-tone classification — this is the exact adjacency the BB-067 revision removed, and it stays removed. Produce 3-5 sample portraits, review with the owner, record the go/no-go in this bead.
- If GO — portrait data format: per-entity, palette-indexed JSON grid, versioned and released with the public projections like any other artifact; renderer: an SVG/canvas component in packages/ui producing crisp large-pixel output at any size (flat matte fills, no smoothing, no effects), with alt text naming the person (guide p.13: alt text names the subject).
- Authoring workflow (manual, per owner direction): a repeatable path from reference image to hand-finished grid — script-assisted quantization to the constrained palette as a starting point, then human cleanup in a simple grid-editing surface; per-portrait provenance recorded (reference source, rights basis of the reference, author, date).
- Living-person policy check BEFORE any authoring: confirm whether depicting living persons is permitted at all under the BB-015 enforcement posture, and record the decision.
- Fallback design for entities without a portrait yet — the system must not make un-portraited people look lesser.

Never (acceptance-level rules):
- No AI-generated likeness presented as documentary material; every shipped portrait is human-authored and human-approved (assistive tooling is fine; a human finishes and signs off).
- No palette framing as skin-tone classification; no palette entry labeled with racial terms.
- No portrait rendered without PERSON / ROLE / PLACE / YEAR context adjacency (guide p.10 "People with context"); never anonymous-portrait decoration.
- No living-person portrait without the recorded policy decision.

Model routing (guidance): opus-class for the spike — recognizability-with-dignity judgment is the entire question; sonnet-class for the renderer, data format, and tooling after a GO; the portrait authoring itself is human work, not model work. If the spike is NO-GO, close the bead with findings and build nothing.
design: Owner intent: photos of everyone are infeasible; a code-built pixelated representation, granular enough to recognize the person, authored manually, could cover everyone. Guardrails from the brand guide p.10: people with context (PERSON/ROLE/PLACE/YEAR), avoid anonymous portraits and AI images presented as documentary. Hard history: BB-067 was revised specifically to remove skin-tone-scale adjacency — the constrained palette here composes portraits and must never be framed or labeled as a skin classification. Living-person depiction needs a BB-015 policy check before any authoring. Precedent for the register: flat matte fills only, no effects — the mark is no longer the only blocky element if this ships, so the spike must also judge brand fit.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Spike delivered: 3-5 sample portraits at candidate grid sizes, owner review held, go/no-go recorded in the bead. 2. If GO: versioned palette-indexed grid format released with public projections; packages/ui renderer with crisp pixels, flat fills, person-naming alt text; authoring workflow documented with per-portrait provenance (reference source, rights basis, author, date). 3. Living-person policy decision recorded before any authoring. 4. Portraits never render without PERSON/ROLE/PLACE/YEAR adjacency; fallback design for un-portraited entities shipped. 5. If NO-GO: findings recorded, bead closed, nothing built.

title: BB-081: Relevance and discovery feedback loop
description:
Expansion bead BB-081 from the 2026-07-17 course-correction review (relevance and discovery feedback loop).

Source: owner brief 2026-07-17 ("weighs things appropriately, considers relevance") + pipeline review
Plan: plan.md
Size: M
Dependencies: BB-040, BB-044, BB-047

Why: the relevance and confidence engines are deterministic and versioned — good — but nothing closes the loop: researcher accept/reject/override decisions are recorded in case history and never systematically compared against what the engines predicted. Without this, weights fossilize and the graylist recall lane never proves whether it catches what matters.

Deliver:
- Decision log: every research-case transition that accepts, rejects, or overrides an engine verdict (BB-044 already has append-only history) is extracted into a calibration dataset — engine scores at decision time vs human disposition, with the input fingerprints BB-043 already stamps.
- Periodic recalibration report (scheduled via BB-084): per-dimension disagreement analysis (which relevance dimensions most often disagree with humans), query-pack effectiveness (BB-038 metrics: which packs produce accepted candidates vs noise), graylist yield (how many parked weak signals were later corroborated — the falls-through-the-cracks metric), and source-tier precision by adapter.
- Human-approved weight changes ONLY: the report proposes; changes ship as versioned policy/config updates (constitution versioning pattern) and must pass the BB-047 gold-corpus gates before taking effect. No silent auto-tuning, no learned ranker — the determinism invariant holds.
- Drift alarms: if live human-vs-engine disagreement exceeds a threshold for a period, raise an operator alert (BB-034 pattern) — the calibration equivalent of schema drift quarantine.
design: The engines are deterministic and versioned but nothing closes the loop today - weights fossilize and the graylist never proves its worth. This is the calibration equivalent of schema-drift quarantine.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Decision log extracted from BB-044 case history: engine scores at decision time vs human disposition, keyed by the BB-043 input fingerprints. 2. Scheduled recalibration report (via BB-084): per-dimension disagreement, query-pack effectiveness, graylist yield (parked weak signals later corroborated - the falls-through-the-cracks metric), source-tier precision by adapter. 3. Weight changes ship ONLY as versioned policy/config updates that pass the BB-047 gold-corpus gates before effect (test proves the config path; no silent tuning, no learned ranker). 4. Drift alarm: sustained human-vs-engine disagreement above threshold raises an operator alert (BB-034 pattern).
notes:
Delivered 2026-07-17: packages/domain/src/relevance-feedback/ — a read-only calibration layer around BB-040's relevance engine and BB-044's research-case history, never a replacement, never a learned ranker. decision-log.ts extracts accept/reject/override transitions from BB-044 case history, pairs each with the engine's score-at-decision-time and a deterministic sha256 input fingerprint (same canonicalize->JSON->sha256 pattern BB-043 established, applied to relevance rather than confidence claims — documented clarification that BB-043's ConfidenceInputFingerprints type is for claims, not relevance candidates, so there's no direct shared type). recalibration-report.ts: per-dimension disagreement ranking, query-pack effectiveness (reuses BB-038's computeEffectivenessMetrics directly), graylist yield (returns available:false with a documented reason — genuinely blocked on BB-073's graylist lane, confirmed via grep, not fabricated), source-tier precision by adapter. weight-policy.ts: proposeWeightChange -> requireGoldCorpusGatePassed -> approveWeightChange with proposer!=approver enforced (mirrors BB-085's promotion-boundary test shape) — a report alone cannot mutate live weights, tested. drift-alarm.ts: pure evaluateRelevanceDriftAlarm, no observability dependency.

Real job wired into BB-084's roster (packages/config/src/scheduled-jobs/jobs/recalibration-report.ts): builds the report + drift evaluation, raises a real BB-034 SEC-SRC-01 alert only when triggered, report-only (never proposes/approves a weight change itself — that's a separate human-triggered path).

Deliberately did NOT touch packages/domain/src/relevance/gates.ts or confidence-engine/engine.ts (multiple other agents were concurrently editing those files this session) — the whole design avoided needing writes there, eliminating shared-file risk entirely. Confirmed after the fact: git diff shows those two files were touched only by other agents.

Not wired: an approved RelevanceWeightPolicy flowing back into the live RELEVANCE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS constant (would require editing relevance/dimensions.ts) — documented as an intentional data-only proposal/approval boundary, a future deploy step not a bug.

Validation (re-run and confirmed by the parent session): pnpm --filter @black-book/domain test 309/309 pass; pnpm --filter @black-book/config test 85/85 pass, typecheck clean. pnpm --filter @black-book/domain typecheck currently shows 3 pre-existing errors in packages/domain/src/adapters/dpla/ and adapters/internet-archive/ — confirmed these belong to BB-073 (still in flight at time of this bead's landing, exactOptionalPropertyTypes issues), not caused by BB-081; will be clean once BB-073 lands its fix.

Zero shared-file collisions (avoided the contested confidence-engine/relevance-engine files by design). 309+85 tests passing.

title: BB-075: Web-search and Common Crawl discovery
description:
Expansion bead BB-075 from the 2026-07-17 course-correction review (web-search and Common Crawl discovery).

Source: owner brief 2026-07-17 + crowdsource-ingestion research (API landscape verified 2026)
Plan: plan.md
Size: M
Dependencies: BB-033, BB-037, BB-073, BB-077

Why: RSS and archive APIs only find sources we already know to watch. Programmatic web search finds the obscure personal blog or church-history page nobody registered. The 2026 landscape is narrow and must be chosen deliberately: Bing Search API retired Aug 2025; Google Programmable Search JSON API is closed to new customers and sunsets Jan 2027 — do not build on either.

Deliver:
- Primary adapter: Brave Search API on the storage-rights plan (base-plan ToS does NOT grant result storage; the storage-rights tier does — get the storage terms confirmed in writing before persisting anything, ~$5/1k queries) OR Exa semantic search (~$7/1k, zero-data-retention posture, strong at "obscure page" discovery; confirm storage terms with sales). Decision recorded on this bead with the confirmation evidence.
- Common Crawl retrospective sweeps (free, AWS Open Data + Hugging Face): CDX-index queries for name/place mentions across historical crawls — the retrospective complement to real-time search; research/fair-use terms match our posture.
- Query generation from BB-038 query packs (period-appropriate terms, researchOnlyOffensive terms never sent to external APIs — check this constraint explicitly), geographically seeded per state/county.
- Budget guards via BB-033 cost controls: per-campaign query budgets, monthly spend caps, alerts; every external query and result stamped with provenance (API, query, timestamp, plan/terms version).
- Results flow into the standard candidate pipeline (BB-039 dedup, BB-040 relevance, graylist for weak signals); discovered URLs go through BB-030 URL safety and the BB-073 Wayback capture layer.

Common Crawl free (AWS Open Data + Hugging Face), CDX-queryable, research/fair-use terms - the retrospective complement.

Discovered URLs flow through BB-030 safety and the BB-073 capture layer into the standard candidate pipeline.

title: BB-074: Reddit discovery adapter (gated channel)
description:
Expansion bead BB-074 from the 2026-07-17 course-correction review (Reddit discovery adapter — gated channel).

Source: owner brief 2026-07-17 + crowdsource-ingestion research (Reddit terms verified against primary sources)
Plan: plan.md
Size: M
Dependencies: BB-037, BB-073, BB-077

Why: Reddit threads (r/AskHistorians, r/BlackHistory, city and state subs) surface leads no archive holds — family histories, neighborhood memory, photo identifications. But Reddit access is now gated and contractually constrained, so this adapter is compliance-first by design.

Access reality (2026): self-service API registration closed under Reddit's Responsible Builder Policy — approval is a ticket queue with a 2-4 week reported lead time; unauthenticated .json endpoints return 403 since May 2026. Free tier: 100 queries/min OAuth, non-commercial use. Reddit for Researchers requires a university-affiliated PI (cleaner dataset path if a partnership exists).

Deliver:
- HUMAN STEP (blocks everything else): submit the Responsible Builder application stating the non-commercial archival-research use case plainly; record the outcome on this bead.
- Polling adapter (registry-governed per BB-037): /new listings for a curated, versioned subreddit list — well within 100 QPM. Structural limits to design around: no date-range search, no comment search, 1000-item listing caps.
- Pointer-first storage: permalink, post ID, subreddit, timestamp, author handle (never resolved to identity), plus a minimal working snippet for reviewer triage only.
- Deletion-sync job (contractual, not optional): scheduled liveness re-check of every stored Reddit pointer; content deleted by the user or Reddit is purged from our stores within 48 hours, including snippets — "even if disassociated, de-identified or anonymized" retention violates the terms. Re-verify liveness immediately before any human review or research-case attachment.
- Hard prohibitions encoded as fail-closed tests: no republication of Reddit content anywhere public (threads are cited as discovery leads that pointed researchers to verifiable primary sources); no ML training on Reddit content; no deanonymization of users.

Constraint: adapter ships fixtures-first and stays in canary until the application is approved; if the application is denied, close this bead with reason and route Reddit leads through the BB-076 manual submission lane instead.
design: Reddit 2026 reality (primary sources): self-service API registration closed under Responsible Builder Policy (ticket queue, 2-4 week lead); unauthenticated .json endpoints return 403 since May 2026; free tier 100 QPM non-commercial; deleted-content retention violates terms even if de-identified (48h purge recommended); structural gaps: no date-range search, no comment search, 1000-item listing caps. Reddit for Researchers needs a university PI - cleaner path if a partnership exists.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Responsible Builder application submitted with the non-commercial archival-research use case; outcome recorded on this bead (HUMAN STEP, blocks the rest). 2. Polling adapter respects the 100 QPM free tier; curated subreddit list is versioned config. 3. Pointer-first storage (permalink, IDs, timestamp, minimal triage snippet; author never resolved to identity). 4. Deletion-sync job purges deleted content within 48 hours including snippets; liveness re-checked immediately before any human review or case attachment. 5. Fail-closed tests: no republication anywhere public, no ML training on Reddit content, no deanonymization. 6. Fixtures-first canary until approval; if denied, close with reason and route Reddit leads through BB-076.

title: bb_reference.jurisdictions.location is NULL for all 3144 counties (loader never writes PostGIS geometry)
description:
load-reference-counties.ts computes county centroids (tiger-gazetteer.ts's
parseGazetteerCountyFile gives INTPTLAT/INTPTLONG per row) but the INSERT in
upsertCounties() only writes id/kind/name/state_fips/county_fips/parent_id/metadata
-- the `location` PostGIS column is never populated. Confirmed: all 3144 county
rows have location IS NULL; the centroid only survives in metadata.geoid, not
as queryable geometry.

Effect: apps/web's resolveDisplayRadiusMeters (geo-precision.ts) has no way to
resolve a jurisdiction bbox for 'county' tier entities (it only special-cases
'locality'+DC and 'state' via US_STATES bbox), so every county-precision
entity's radius-affordance circle reports "unavailable" instead of rendering
an actual circle. Not misleading (no fake circle drawn) but an incomplete
feature -- first surfaced by the NRHP county-centroid reconciliation
(repo-jy6k, packages/ops-data/scripts/reconcile-nrhp-county-locations.ts).

Fix: add `location = ST_MakePoint($lng, $lat)` (or similar) to the INSERT/
UPDATE in load-reference-counties.ts's upsertCounties(), backfill the existing
3144 rows, then wire resolveDisplayRadiusMeters to look up the county
jurisdiction bbox the same way it already does for 'state'.

title: Statistical observations model: series/observations/derived measurements with uncertainty
description: Demographic statistics must not be ordinary entity claims. Add statisticalSeries/{seriesId} (metricId, definition, universe, unit, sourceDataset/table/variable, geographyType, estimateType, periodType), statisticalObservations/{observationId} (seriesId, jurisdictionId, boundaryVersion, referencePeriod, datasetVintage, estimate, marginOfError, standardError, numerator/denominator, sourceItemId, retrievedAt, status: observed), derivedMeasurements/{measurementId} (methodId+version, inputObservationIds, value, uncertainty, formula, assumptions, status: derived|modeled), modelDefinitions. Combination rules: sum counts only over disjoint geographies + same universe + compatible product/vintage; preserve MOE/SE; store exact source variables; require boundary/crosswalk version (ties to repo-57f43f71 FIPS changes). Growth records store start/end observation ids + significanceResult — no meaningful-looking percent when estimates are statistically indistinguishable (ACS MOE guidance). Three explicit states observed/derived/modeled; never silently fill missing values; interpolation is modeled-only and labeled. Aligns repo-4274f931 (census county decades, in progress) and is the target model for the P3 external-data ingest beads (CDC/EPA/HUD/FCC/etc.).
acceptance_criteria: Schemas + rules for all four collections; combination-rule validators with tests (disjoint-geography sum, universe mismatch rejection, MOE propagation, significance test); repo-4274f931 data expressible in the model; one existing ingest bead retargeted as consumer.
close_reason: Added StatisticalSeries/StatisticalObservation/DerivedMeasurement model (packages/domain/src/statistics/) with combination-rules validators: disjoint-geography summation (boundaryVersion-aware, generalizing the tractVintage constraint), MOE/SE propagation (sqrt-sum-of-squares per Census ACS handbook), and growth-significance testing via non-overlapping confidence intervals. 18 unit tests, domain typecheck clean.

title: Black Book Data Pack v1: signed external dataset contract + quarantine import pipeline

Validation: JSON Schema 2020-12 structural, controlled-vocab, reference resolution; PROV-style lineage. VERIFIED reusable infra: canonical JSON + SHA-256 (packages/domain/src/provenance/hashes.ts:7-44) and ECDSA-signed immutable manifests (packages/firebase/src/firestore/release-activation.ts:33-47) — generalize these, do not build a second security model. New collections: externalDatasets, externalDatasetVersions, datasetSubscriptions, importBatches, importValidationFindings, importQuarantine. Import steps: fetch immutable version, verify checksum+signature, size/count budgets, license check, schema + vocab + reference validation, PII/precision scan, entity resolution against canonical ids (external ids stay namespaced, never auto-canonical), duplicate/contradiction detection, quarantine failures, promote via normal research pipeline. Also publish Black Book's own validated dataset in the same format.
acceptance_criteria: Pack spec v1 documented + JSON Schemas; import pipeline with all quarantine gates and tests; signing generalized from existing infra; a round-trip demo: export own data as a pack, re-import it clean.

External ids always namespaced to their source dataset, never auto-promoted to a canonical id. Added Firestore schema stubs for externalDatasets/externalDatasetVersions/datasetSubscriptions/importBatches/importValidationFindings/importQuarantine. 1096/1096 domain tests passed, both packages typecheck clean.

title: Map street-level rebuild: full basemap, cities, mobile sheets, clustering polish
description:
Expansion bead from the 2026-07-18 blap redesign brief (docs/ui/blap-design-direction-v4.md §5 is the binding spec).

Source: owner brief 2026-07-18 ('the map has to be first class as users may be using this to visit places they find here' + 'rip whatever needs to be ripped').
Size: XL
Dependencies: none hard; census choropleth (repo-4274f931) and address search layer on top of this basemap.

Why: readers will physically visit the places they find — a marker on a Montgomery corner, Vernon AME in Greenwood, a Nashville campus. The current boundaries-only ink plate with a z12 ceiling cannot orient a person on foot. The archive look survives as a STYLE applied to real geography, not a ceiling on it.

Deliver:
- Self-hostable vector basemap (Protomaps PMTiles preferred; OpenFreeMap acceptable — free-first, no per-tile vendor fees, no API-key lock-in) served from our infra, restyled into the archive treatment: ink plate, muted street casings + names, city/neighborhood place labels, civic anchors; commercial POI noise suppressed. National frame to street level (maxZoom 18).
- City labeling at locality zooms from the same tiles (replaces nothing — state labels stay; the archive stays the subject, streets are context).
- Keep the persistent-canvas architecture (ADR-017), camera presets, kind-encoded circles, county/state hairline system, cluster expansion, density tiers — these ride ON the new basemap unchanged.
- Mobile: consolidate explore floating panels into bottom sheets; one-handed reach; 44px+ targets at street zooms; glare-legible in both themes (on-site use).
- Clustering polish at the new zoom range (spiderfy or expansion behavior past clusterMaxZoom where multiple records share a building).
- Performance: PMTiles range requests, tile cache headers, cold-load budget measured at 375px mid-tier device.

Never: per-tile commercial vendor dependency as the only path; POI/commercial clutter; losing the dignity rules at street zoom (public precision still governs — street-level BASEMAP does not mean street-level RECORD precision for redacted records); breaking reduced-motion.

Acceptance:
1. A visitor at z17 in Montgomery can read street names and orient to the Rosa Parks arrest-site marker record with the archive visual language intact. 2. All 104+ release records render on the new basemap with existing encodings; clusters decompose within two interactions everywhere. 3. Explore panels become bottom sheets at <=48rem, verified 375px both themes. 4. Basemap serves from our own hosting with no per-request vendor fees. 5. Lighthouse/trace budget recorded at national frame and street zoom. 6. BB-051 dignity re-verified at street zooms.

Model routing: strong model for basemap style authoring + sheet UX; fast model for tile-hosting plumbing and config.
notes: Human bar applies (docs/ui/blap-design-direction-v4.md §2b, owner 2026-07-18): finding paths, context-carrying transitions, voice-written states, smoothness, one-tap payoff — judged alongside this bead's own acceptance list.

value: WebKit grid layout: never put percentage min-height on a grid item (incl. ::before) that spans an auto-sized row — WebKit resolves the % against the container the item inflates, causing runaway row growth (thousands of px, grows every relayout). gap-fill-hbcu-founding-name-duplicates: The gap-fill candidate scanner (find-catalog-entity-gaps.ts) generates a HIGH rate of duplicate candidates for HBCUs already in packages/firebase/fixtures/national-catalog/hbcu.json — it picks up the institution's HISTORICAL/FOUNDING name (e.g. 'Walden Seminary', 'Atlanta Baptist Female Seminary', 'Institute for Colored Youth', 'Centenary Biblical Institute', 'Augusta Institute', 'State Normal School for Colored Persons', 'Connectional School for the Education of Negro Youth') as a NEW candidate stub because that name appears in another record's claim text mentioning the institution's origin story, without recognizing the name resolves to an ALREADY-CATALOGED entity under its modern name (Philander Smith College, Spelman College, Cheyney University, Morgan State University, Morehouse College, Kentucky State University, Paul Quinn College, Grambling State University, Coppin State University, Central State University all hit this during the 2026-07-19/20 paid-model gap-fill run). Observed rate: roughly half of all 'keep' decisions in HBCU-adjacent chunks were this exact pattern. classifyLeadAgainstCatalog / buildCatalogMatchIndex evidently does not catch historical-name aliases. Mitigation used manually this run: before publishing any gap-fill batch, grep the candidate's displayName (and any name mentioned in its founding claim) against existing national-catalog/*.json displayNames, and check whether the EXISTING entry's summary opening sentence already tells the same founding story verbatim — if so, exclude as duplicate rather than publish. Real fix for a future session: add historical/former-name aliases to the catalog match index (many HBCUs have a well-known founding name distinct from their current name) so find-catalog-entity-gaps.ts stops generating these stubs in the first place.

repo-hol1 FIXED + root cause. The 'eyJtZXVyaWNJ' placeholder was not a hand-typo — ingest-phase2-census-historical-income.ts computed content_hash as Buffer.from(JSON).toString('base64').slice(0,12), which (a) isn't a hash and (b) truncates inside the shared '{"metricI' JSON prefix, so ALL 222 rows across 4 metrics (census-h5 income black + white-nh, census-p2 poverty black + white-nh) got the byte-identical placeholder in CANONICAL bb_reference.statistical_observations, not just fixtures. Fix: (1) ingest now uses observationContentHash = sha256hex(JSON.stringify({metricId, referencePeriod, estimate})) — full 64-char, reproducible from the stored row; (2) new backfill-census-income-hashes.ts (safe-by-default, --commit) rewrote all 222 canonical rows (verified 0 bad remain); (3) 4 fixture hashes fixed to match DB: wealth-gap incomeBlack1972=23170beb.., incomeWhite1972 (spine ref, bound to underlying white-nh 1972 census)=a813fa45.., buying-a-home black1985=aecca671.., white-nh1985=f63528bc... Note: BLS-unemployment ingest uses sha256hex.slice(0,16) (16-char, not 64) — not caught because no packet references it, but it's an inconsistency worth normalizing later.

divine-nine-discovery-2026-07-20: Built discover-divine-nine.ts sourcing NPHC's 9 orgs + Wikidata P112 founders directly (not category-scraping, which pulls mostly-duplicate famous alumni). Wikidata P112 founder claims are frequently incomplete (only got 18 founder QIDs total across 9 orgs vs ~90+ real documented founders) -- fine for closing the 'orgs themselves' gap but not a complete founders roster. Found+fixed 2 real corroborate-source.ts location-resolution bugs live: (1) isUsableLocationLabel only rejected exact generic strings like 'headquarters', missed scope-qualified variants like 'International headquarters' which searched literally and hit an unrelated page instead of falling back to jurisdiction -- fixed with a last-word check. (2) judge sometimes writes a full descriptive clause as locationLabel ('Cornell University, site of Alpha Phi Alpha founding') instead of a bare name; added stripDescriptiveLocationClause to drop the clause when it contains phrases like 'site of'/'home of' while preserving real 'Place, State' qualifiers. Both covered by regression tests in corroborate-source.test.ts, benefit all future campaigns via the shared lib.

reconstruction-officeholders-and-lynching-2026-07-20: Two more 'find the authoritative Wikipedia list, parse it directly' candidates identified 2026-07-20, same pattern as sundown towns. (1) LAUNCHED: 'African American officeholders from the end of the Civil War until before 1900' — 1,927 bulleted names (1,580 unique), clean simple list format like sundown towns, ALL pre-1900 so zero living-status privacy concern — used auto-promote-person-review.ts with an EMPTY exclude list rather than the standard auto-promote-corsair-keeps.ts (which would hold every person-kind entity regardless). Chunked via scripts/chunked-officeholders.sh. discover-reconstruction-officeholders.ts is the extraction script, committed. (2) BUILT AND LAUNCHED: 'List of lynching victims in the United States' — discover-lynching-victims.ts, committed. This one genuinely needed a real rowspan-aware wikitable parser (11 era-tables, 828 total rows, ethnicity/city/county/state/date/accusation frequently shared across consecutive victims via rowspan cells) — verified correctness against real 2-row and 8-row rowspan groups in a Python prototype (exact 547-candidate match between prototype and the TS port) before trusting it at scale. Filtered to African American victims only (article also covers ~1,300 White victims) and drops any row missing a state value (2 of 549 — genuine source-data gaps, not parser bugs) rather than guess. Also chunked via scripts/chunked-lynching-victims.sh, using auto-promote-person-review.ts (all victims are historical/deceased, zero privacy concern). Both pipelines run detached and independently on Corsair in parallel with each other — confirmed tonight's established pattern handles multiple concurrent chunked pipelines fine.

sundown-towns-discovery-2026-07-20: Built discover-sundown-towns.ts to find sundown towns for BlackStory — discover-candidates.ts's keyword filter (looksRelevant, checks title+short Wikidata description) can't find these since a town's description ('city in Illinois') never mentions race even when its documented sundown-town history is extensive. Real fix: found the authoritative source first (Wikipedia's 'List of sundown towns in the United States', a single well-cited article organized by state, one bulleted town per entry with its own Loewen/newspaper citation) and parsed IT directly rather than searching per-town. Output matches build-gap-fill-enrichment-subjects.ts's candidate shape exactly, so the rest of the pipeline (research/judge/promote/publish) needed zero changes. Yield: 160 towns extracted, 133 kept by the paid-model judge, 118 published after removing 1 duplicate (a town already covered from a different angle). This is a MUCH higher signal-to-noise ratio than the original gap-fill mention-scanning approach (which was ~50% duplicates of the existing curated catalog) since it's a genuinely new topic area with independently-documented entries, not name-variants of already-cataloged institutions. Bug fixed before trusting it: MediaWiki <ref>{{cite web|...}} citation templates often span multiple wikitext lines — line-by-line processing left an unclosed <ref> tag leaking into the extracted evidence text; fixed by accumulating a bullet's full multi-line block before stripping markup. General lesson for future topic-specific discovery asks: when the topic's relevance signal lives in article BODY text rather than title/short-description, look for Wikipedia's own authoritative list/category article on the topic and parse that directly instead of trying to tune keyword search.

shared-worktree-git-hazard: RECURRED REPEATEDLY on 2026-07-19/20 during a long gap-fill-research session — a SEPARATE, concurrently-running agent session (not an unattended automation this time) actively checks out main and commits real feature work on this SAME primary checkout at /Users/geralddagher/Developer/Projects/blackstory at least 5+ times in one session, sometimes mid-edit. Confirmed 'git worktree add' for the SAME branch name is blocked by git when that branch is already checked out elsewhere, so it is not always a usable mitigation. Practical pattern that worked repeatedly without data loss: before any git operation, run 'git branch --show-current' and 'git status --short' first; if uncommitted work is not on the intended branch, 'git stash push -m <label> -- <specific files>' (pathspec-scoped, not a blanket stash) then checkout the correct branch then 'git stash pop'; expect merge conflicts when the stash's base commit and the target branch have diverged on the same lines (harmless — resolve by inspecting both sides, they are often genuinely complementary edits from different work, not real conflicts) BUT ALSO expect the pop to sometimes span unrelated file pairs (e.g. .beads/issues.jsonl) that were never intentionally stashed together — resolve those with 'git checkout --ours' since beads' JSONL export is a non-deterministic-order regenerated mirror of Dolt state, not the source of truth. Commit and push immediately after resolving, per-file, rather than batching. When work is deployed to a remote host (e.g. Corsair) independent of the local checkout, remote deployment state is NOT affected by local branch thrashing — verify the remote copy directly instead of trusting local git state as a proxy for what is actually running.

location-backfill-pattern-2026-07-20: Built resolveGovernmentCenterCoordinates() in packages/firebase/scripts/lib/corroborate-source.ts to backfill real coordinates for gap-fill subjects the judge already located in text (jurisdictionLabel/locationLabel) but which lacked Wikidata coordinates on their own Wikipedia article. Dispatches on locationPrecision (not fuzzy string matching, which is unreliable — 'New York' is both a city and state name): named site/institution/address first, then government center (state capitol via Wikipedia search, U.S. Capitol for locationPrecision=='country'), then the jurisdiction/location text itself. Real bugs found and fixed during live testing before trusting it at scale: (1) loose state-substring matching anchored 'New York, New York' to Albany instead of NYC — fixed by requiring EXACT bare-state match gated on locationPrecision=='state'; (2) blind top-search-hit resolved 'Lake City Public Library' (Lake City, SC) to a same-named building in Salt Lake City, UT — fixed by appending a state disambiguator to search queries; (3) generic labels like 'headquarters'/'site' searched literally matched unrelated pages — now skipped in favor of jurisdictionLabel.
